**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 647, MECA-79 (HEV-specific)+Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected for its excellent clearing of dense lymphoid organs like lymph nodes (2-3 mm), strong preservation of antibody-derived fluorescence (crucial for detecting HEV-specific MECA-79 and pan-endothelial CD31), and compatibility with organic solvent-based refractive index matching for high-resolution 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). The methanol series effectively dehydrates and permeabilizes the tissue for deep antibody penetration. The labeling strategy uses: 1) **MECA-79 antibody** (not in the provided list but is the canonical marker for HEV peripheral node addressing, essential for the scientific goal) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 to specifically highlight the high endothelial venule network. 2) **CD31 (PECAM1) antibody** conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 to label all vascular endothelium, providing the overall vascular architecture as a spatial reference. 3) **Hoechst** nuclear dye to label all nuclei, delineating lymphocyte-dense zones (cortex/follicles) and medullary regions.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Sample Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed lymph node twice in PBS for 30 minutes each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 6% normal donkey serum in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

2  Immunostaining
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail (Rat anti-MECA-79 at 1:100, Armenian Hamster anti-CD31 at 1:100 in blocking solution) for 7 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.2 Wash with wash buffer (0.2% Tween-20, 10 μg/mL Heparin in PBS) 6 times over 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail (Donkey anti-Rat IgG Alexa Fluor 555 at 1:500, Donkey anti-Armenian Hamster IgG Alexa Fluor 647 at 1:500 in blocking solution) for 7 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.4 Wash with wash buffer 6 times over 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Incubation with nuclear stain (5 μg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBS) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

3  Dehydration and Delipidation
3.1 Incubation with a graded methanol series in PBS: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol (vol/vol), each for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours)
3.2 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes MeOH) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 100% methanol twice, each for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 66% Dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% Methanol (vol/vol) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.5 Incubation with 100% DCM twice, each for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours minimum, can store for imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素), CD31 (PECAM1), Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO provides excellent transparency and strong shrinkage (ideal for the small, dense lymph node), superior preservation of endogenous fluorescence (crucial for any potential reporter signals), and compatibility with lipophilic dyes and antibody labeling. Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum lectin) broadly labels vascular endothelium, including HEVs. Anti-CD31 (PECAM1) antibody specifically labels all vascular endothelial cells, allowing segmentation of the general vasculature. The differential signal (Lectin+ CD31+) helps identify the specialized HEV segments. 1.2 Incubation in blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 1% BSA, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 6 hours at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
1.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: Anti-CD31 (Rat anti-mouse, 1:200) and Biotinylated Lycopersicon esculentum Lectin (1:100) in blocking solution for 48 hours at 4°C with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.4 Wash sample with PBST 6 times, 1 hour each wash, at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Donkey anti-Rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Streptavidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in blocking solution for 48 hours at 4°C with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.6 Wash sample with PBST 6 times, 1 hour each wash, at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)
1.7 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (5 µg/mL) in PBS for 2 hours at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.8 Wash sample with PBS 3 times, 30 minutes each wash, at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Incubation in a graded methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol (vol/vol in H2O), 1 hour per step at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)
2.2 Incubation in fresh 100% methanol overnight at 4°C with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

3  uDISCO Clearing
3.1 Incubation in 66% Dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% Methanol (vol/vol) for 3 hours at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.2 Incubation in 100% Dichloromethane (DCM) for 15 minutes at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.3 Incubation in Diethyl Ether (freshly opened) for 15 minutes at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.4 Incubation in uDISCO clearing solution: Diphenyl Ether (DPE) with 1,2-Diphenoxyethane (15% vol/vol as antioxidant) until the sample is fully transparent (typically 2-4 hours for a 2-3 mm sample). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

4.1 Transfer the cleared sample into a fresh vial containing pure uDISCO clearing solution (DPE with antioxidant). The solution's RI (~1.56) is suitable for imaging with high-NA objectives. (Temperature: RT, Time: Storage until imaging)
4.2 Mount the sample in a custom or commercial imaging chamber filled with uDISCO clearing solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: Ready for imaging)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Anti-CD31 (PECAM1) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, Anti-Podoplanin (PDPN) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing of small, dense lymphoid tissues (2-3 mm), achieving high transparency and minimal size change, which is crucial for precise 3D spatial analysis. It offers excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-conjugated fluorophores (Alexa Fluor dyes). The labeling strategy targets HEVs (CD31/PECAM1 for pan-endothelial marker, PDPN for lymphatic endothelial marker to help distinguish HEV morphology), while Hoechst stains all nuclei, clearly delineating lymphocyte-dense cortical and paracortical zones. This combination allows for the co-localization analysis of the HEV network relative to cellular compartments without requiring complex intracellular lymphocyte markers for the primary goal.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Sample Preparation and Staining
1.1 Wash fixed lymph node sample in PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 (PBS-T) for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Block and permeabilize in PBS containing 5% normal goat serum and 0.3% Triton X-100 for 12 hours at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody cocktail: Anti-CD31-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) and Anti-Podoplanin-Alexa Fluor 555 (1:200) in PBS containing 1% normal goat serum and 0.1% Triton X-100 for 48 hours at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
1.4 Wash sample in PBS-T for 6 hours, changing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
1.5 Incubate with nuclear stain: 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBS for 12 hours at room temperature protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.6 Wash sample in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Dehydrate through a graded methanol series in PBS: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol (vol/vol), each for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)
2.2 Incubate in fresh 100% methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubate in 66% Dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% Methanol (vol/vol) for 3 hours at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.4 Incubate in 100% DCM for 15 minutes at room temperature with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

3  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubate in DiBenzyl Ether (DBE) for refractive index matching and final clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
3.2 Transfer cleared sample to fresh DBE for storage and imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)

It provides excellent delipidation and transparency for small, dense lymphoid organs (2–3 mm lymph nodes) while maintaining antigenicity. The methanol and DCM steps effectively reduce autofluorescence and non-specific background. The chosen labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goals: Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-CD31 for pan-endothelial visualization, Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated MECA-79 antibody for HEV-specific addressin (PNAd), DAPI for nuclear reference and lymphocyte-dense zone delineation, and Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated IB4 lectin as an additional vascular endothelial marker to enhance vascular network contrast and provide structural context. **Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Pre-treatment  
1.1 Wash fixed lymph node twice with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated once)  

2  Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Rehydration through a descending methanol series in PBST: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  
2.3 Wash with PBST three times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

3.1 Blocking and permeabilization in PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum and 0.3% Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rat anti-mouse CD31 (1:200), rat anti-mouse PNAd (MECA-79, 1:100), and biotinylated IB4 lectin (1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)  
3.3 Wash with PBST six times over 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours each)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC)+Alexa Fluor 647, CD169 (Siglec-1)+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]

The labeling strategy uses B220 (pan-B cell marker) to specifically highlight B cell follicles, CD169 to demarcate marginal zone macrophages (defining the white/red pulp boundary), and DAPI for nuclear reference. This combination allows precise mapping of follicle location, size, number, and spatial arrangement relative to splenic anatomical landmarks.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Permeabilization and Blocking
1.1 Wash fixed spleen twice with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-Tx). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Wash with PBS-Tx twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
1.4 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2  Immunostaining
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rat anti-mouse B220 (clone RA3-6B2) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) and rat anti-mouse CD169 (clone 3D6.112) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (1:200) in PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 10 μg/mL heparin, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (PBSH-TwD). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Wash with PBSH-TwD four times. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour each)
2.3 Incubation with DAPI (5 μg/mL) in PBSH-TwD. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Wash with PBSH-TwD twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

3  Dehydration
3.1 Incubation with a graded methanol series in distilled water: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol, each step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
3.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

4  Delipidation and Bleaching
4.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes methanol). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

5  Refractive Index Matching
5.1 Incubation with a graded series of dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol: 33%, 66%, 100% (vol/vol) DCM, each step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
5.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
5.3 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220 (PTPRC), Lectin (IB4), DAPI]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected for its excellent clearing of dense lymphoid organs like the spleen, its compatibility with whole-organ processing (~15 mm size), and its strong preservation of antibody and lectin fluorescence through organic solvent-based steps. The labeling strategy targets B cells directly with B220 (a pan-B cell marker), uses IB4 lectin to label high endothelial venules and stromal networks which can delineate germinal center regions, and employs DAPI for nuclear counterstain to assess cellular density and architecture. This combination allows for clear 3D visualization of B cell follicles, identification of germinal center-like structures via lectin pattern, and quantitative spatial analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2  Bleaching and Rehydration
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12-24 hours)
2.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)
2.3 Rehydration through a graded methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
2.4 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBTx).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)

3  Immunostaining and Lectin Labeling
3.1 Blocking with PBTx containing 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 10 µg/mL Lectin from *Griffonia simplicifolia* (IB4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24-48 hours)
3.2 Primary antibody incubation in blocking solution with anti-B220 antibody (e.g., clone RA3-6B2, 1:200 dilution) and 10 µg/mL IB4 lectin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
3.3 Wash with PBTx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)
3.4 Secondary antibody incubation in PBTx with donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 dilution) and 10 µg/mL IB4 lectin.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
3.5 Wash with PBTx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)
3.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBTx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
3.7 Wash with PBTx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)

4  Dehydration for Clearing
4.1 Dehydration through a graded methanol series in PBS: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)

5  Delipidation and Clearing
5.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
5.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
5.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)

6  Refractive Index Matching
6.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24-48 hours until sample is transparent)

**Chosen Labeling:** [B220+Alexa Fluor 488, CD3+Alexa Fluor 647, Ki67+Alexa Fluor 594, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS (Polyethylene glycol‑Associated Solvent System) is selected because it effectively clears large, dense, and highly pigmented organs like the spleen. It combines strong decolorization (removing heme) and delipidation while preserving endogenous and antibody‑induced fluorescence across multiple channels. The method uses a graded series of tert‑butanol and BABB‑D5, which efficiently removes hemoglobin and lipids, resulting in a transparent, low‑background sample ideal for 3D light‑sheet imaging of intact spleen architecture. The chosen markers: B220 (pan‑B cell) defines follicles, CD3 (T cell) helps delineate peri‑arteriolar lymphoid sheaths (PALS), and Ki67 marks proliferating cells in germinal centers; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain. This combination allows precise 3D mapping of follicle size, number, volume, and germinal‑center activity without requiring extra fluorophores outside the allowed list.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  **Decolorization & Dehydration**  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) tert‑butanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) tert‑butanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) tert‑butanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) tert‑butanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert‑butanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with one solution change after 12 hours)

2  **Delipidation & Bleaching**  
2.1 Incubation with fresh BABB‑D5 solution (1 part benzyl alcohol, 2 parts benzyl benzoate, 0.4% (vol/vol) diphenyl ether).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours, with one solution change after 24 hours)

3  **Rehydration & Permeabilization**  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) tert‑butanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) tert‑butanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

4  **Immunolabeling**  
4.1 Blocking with PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum and 0.1% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

请根据该科学问题自行选择合适的荧光/标记策略，并基于所选标记样本选择匹配的组织透明方法。若限制范围内的核染料只能提供细胞密度或肿瘤结构参考，则不应替代 T 细胞身份标记。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3+Alexa Fluor 647, CD8+Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO provides excellent transparency and shrinkage for dense, lipid-rich tissues like tumors, achieving high refractive index (RI ~1.56) ideal for high-resolution imaging. Its organic solvent-based process effectively removes lipids while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody signals over long periods, crucial for analyzing large (~8mm) samples. The chosen labeling strategy uses CD3 to identify all T cells and CD8 to specifically label cytotoxic T cells, enabling the quantitative analysis of total and cytotoxic T-cell infiltration densities and spatial patterns. Hoechst provides nuclear counterstaining for defining tissue architecture and cellular density without interfering with the specific T-cell markers.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tetrahydrofuran (THF) in distilled water.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) THF in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, repeated twice)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2  Immunofluorescence Labeling
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization by incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, and 3% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin (BSA).(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Primary antibody incubation with a cocktail of rat anti-mouse CD3 (1:200) and rabbit anti-mouse CD8α (1:200) in PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 3% (wt/vol) BSA.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.3 Washing by incubation with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, repeated three times)
2.4 Secondary antibody incubation with a cocktail of donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in PBST containing 3% (wt/vol) BSA.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.5 Washing by incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, repeated three times)
2.6 Nuclear staining by incubation with 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.7 Final wash by incubation with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, repeated three times)
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, until tissue is fully transparent)

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)  
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

2  Immunostaining  
2.1 Rehydration through graded methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol in PBS, each step.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated three times)  
2.3 Blocking with PBS-T containing 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 10 µg/ml anti-CD16/32.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rat anti-CD3 (1:200) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 and rat anti-CD8 (1:200) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.5 Wash with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated four times)  
2.6 Incubation with nuclear stain: 1 µg/ml Hoechst 33342 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.7 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)  

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing  
3.1 Dehydration through graded methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol in PBS, each step.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)  
3.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

4.1 Transfer cleared sample to fresh DBE in an imaging-compatible chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3+Alexa Fluor 488, CD8+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31+Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its excellent transparency of large, dense tissues (up to cm-scale), strong preservation of endogenous and antibody-conjugated fluorescence, and compatibility with whole-mount immunolabeling. Its organic-solvent-based dehydration and delipidation efficiently clear lipid-rich tumor tissue while maintaining structural integrity. The labeling strategy uses CD3 (pan-T cell) and CD8 (cytotoxic T cell) antibodies to distinguish T-cell subpopulations, CD31 for vascular reference, and Hoechst for nuclear architecture. This combination allows precise 3D mapping of T-cell infiltration gradients between tumor core and margin.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour, repeated twice. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours each)
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2  Immunolabeling
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization with PTxwH solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.1% Tween-20, 10% DMSO, 5% normal donkey serum) for 2 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Primary antibody incubation in PTxwH solution containing: anti-CD3 (1:200, Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate), anti-CD8 (1:200, Alexa Fluor 647 conjugate), anti-CD31 (1:100, Alexa Fluor 555 conjugate). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.3 Wash with PTxwH solution, 6 changes over 2 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.4 Nuclear staining with Hoechst 33342 (2 µg/mL) in PTxwH solution for 2 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Wash with PTxwH solution, 3 changes over 1 day. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD3+Alexa Fluor 488, CD8+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 555]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected over the previously used iDISCO+ for several reasons critical to the problem statement. It provides superior transparency for dense, lipid-rich tissues like solid tumors, enabling imaging of the core. It offers excellent fluorescence preservation for Alexa Fluor dyes (which are more photostable than many fluorescent proteins) through its tetrahydrofuran (THF) and dibenzyl ether (DBE) solvent series. The protocol includes an effective decolorization step (using H2O2 in methanol) to reduce tissue autofluorescence, a key requirement given the weak signal issue. The solvent-based nature ensures rapid and deep antibody penetration for whole 8 mm tumors. The chosen markers (CD3 for pan-T cells, CD8 for cytotoxic T cells, DAPI for nuclei, and Lectin for vasculature) directly address the scientific goal of mapping T cell subsets relative to tumor regions and vasculature without introducing extraneous targets.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Decolorization and Dehydration
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with a second change of 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12-24 hours)

2  Rehydration and Permeabilization
2.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBTx).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 3 times)
2.6 Incubation with PBTx containing 20% (vol/vol) DMSO and 2.3% (wt/vol) glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12-24 hours)

3  Blocking and Immunostaining
3.1 Incubation with PBTx containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, and 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide (Blocking Solution).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in Blocking Solution: rat anti-mouse CD3 (1:200) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488, rat anti-mouse CD8a (1:200) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, and biotinylated Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum, 1:100).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72-96 hours with gentle shaking)
3.3 Wash with PBTx.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeat 6 times over 24 hours)
3.4 Incubation with secondary/tertiary staining cocktail in Blocking Solution: Streptavidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) and DAPI (1:1000).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48-72 hours with gentle shaking)
3.5 Wash with PBTx.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeat 6 times over 24 hours)

4  Final Dehydration and Solvent Clearing
4.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 2 times)
4.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
4.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeat 2 times)
4.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ~1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours or until fully transparent, store in DBE for imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40/Hcn4 (primary antibody), Alexa Fluor 647 (secondary antibody), DAPI (nuclear counterstain), Lectin (vascular reference)]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its ability to rapidly clear dense, blood-rich tissues (like the fixed mouse heart) while strongly preserving endogenous and antibody-induced fluorescence over long periods. It achieves high transparency and high refractive index (RI ~1.56) suitable for high-resolution light-sheet imaging of the entire heart. The chosen labeling strategy uses Cx40/Hcn4 (a well-established marker for Purkinje fibers in the cardiac conduction system) to specifically highlight the target network, DAPI for general nuclear architecture, and Lectin (e.g., IB4) to outline blood vessels as an anatomical reference without interfering with the primary Purkinje fiber signal.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Sample Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed heart sample in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 20% (vol/vol) DMSO) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

2  Immunostaining and Counterstaining
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody solution (rabbit anti-Cx40/Hcn4, 1:500 in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 5% DMSO, and 3% normal donkey serum) for 7 days. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.2 Wash with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100) for 24 hours, refreshing solution 4 times. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody solution (donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647, 1:500, and DyLight 488-conjugated Lectin (IB4), 1:200, in the same diluent as step 2.1) for 7 days. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.4 Wash with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100) for 24 hours, refreshing solution 4 times. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Incubation with DAPI solution (1 µg/mL in PBST) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.6 Final wash with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

3  Dehydration and Solvent-Based Clearing
3.1 Gradual dehydration in methanol/water series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in water, each step for 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 10 hours total)
3.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.5 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ~1.56) for refractive index matching and final clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4  Storage and Imaging
4.1 Store cleared heart in fresh DBE in a light-tight container at 4 ℃ until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: long-term)
4.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber for light-sheet microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40 (Connexin 43) + Alexa Fluor 647, Cntn2 + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its excellent clearing capability and strong preservation of endogenous fluorescence (e.g., GFP/YFP) and antibody-derived signals in large, dense tissues like the whole mouse heart. It achieves high transparency and a high refractive index (RI ~1.56), ideal for deep-tissue imaging of fine structures like Purkinje fibers. The labeling strategy uses specific antibodies against Cx40 (a key gap junction protein in the cardiac conduction system) and Cntn2 (Contactin-2, a marker associated with Purkinje fiber-related contact proteins) to directly identify the target networks. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for overall tissue architecture. This combination allows for precise dual-channel visualization and spatial co-localization analysis of the two protein signals within the 3D context of the cleared heart.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed heart sample in PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 (PBS-T) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100 and 0.05% Tween-20) for 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

2  Immunostaining
2.1 Blocking with solution containing 10% normal donkey serum and 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS for 48 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: Rabbit anti-Cx40 (1:200) and Chicken anti-Cntn2 (1:100) in blocking solution for 7 days.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.3 Wash with PBS-T for 48 hours, refreshing solution every 12 hours.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Donkey anti-Rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Donkey anti-Chicken IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution for 7 days.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.5 Wash with PBS-T for 48 hours, refreshing solution every 12 hours.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS for 24 hours.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.7 Final wash with PBS for 12 hours.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

3  Dehydration
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in deionized water for 3 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in deionized water for 3 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in deionized water for 3 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 6 hours, refreshing once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

4  Delipidation and Clearing
4.1 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM) for 3 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
4.2 Incubation with fresh dibenzyl ether (DBE) for 3 hours to achieve final clearing and refractive index matching (RI ~1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

5  Storage and Imaging
5.1 Store cleared heart sample in fresh DBE in a light-tight container at 4 ℃ until imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite)
5.2 Mount sample in a custom chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Cx40/Hcn4 (for Purkinje fibers), Lectin (for vasculature), Hoechst (for nuclei)]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency and significant tissue shrinkage (up to 65% in volume), which is advantageous for imaging a dense organ like the whole mouse heart. The shrinkage improves imaging depth and resolution while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody signals well. The method is compatible with whole-organ immunolabeling and provides a stable, hydrophobic clearing medium suitable for long-term storage and high-resolution light-sheet imaging. Cx40/Hcn4 is a specific marker for the cardiac conduction system (including Purkinje fibers). Lectin outlines the vasculature, and Hoechst stains nuclei, together providing essential anatomical references for spatial registration.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2  Immunolabeling (Optional perfusion of dyes can be performed prior to fixation; here assuming post-fixed whole-heart immunostaining)  
2.1 Rehydration through a methanol series: 80%, 50%, 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, each step 1 hour at RT.  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T) 3 × 1 hour at RT.  
2.3 Blocking with PBS-T containing 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 10 mg/mL bovine serum albumin (BSA). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-Cx40 (1:200) and biotinylated Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum, 1:100) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.5 Wash with PBS-T 6 × 2 hours at RT.  
2.6 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.7 Wash with PBS-T 6 × 2 hours at RT.  
2.8 Incubation with 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.9 Wash with PBS 3 × 1 hour at RT.  

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing  
3.1 Dehydration through a methanol series: 30%, 50%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS, each step 1 hour at RT.  
3.2 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
3.4 Clearing and RI matching: Incubation with pure dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, or until tissue is transparent)  

4  Storage and Imaging  
4.1 Store cleared heart in fresh DBE in a light-tight container at 4 ℃ until imaging.  
4.2 For imaging, mount sample in DBE-compatible chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat twice)
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Diethyl Ether (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Collagen IV+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and antibody labeling exceptionally well, making it ideal for multi-target immunofluorescence in whole organs. It achieves high transparency in dense tissues like kidney and maintains structural integrity for accurate 3D reconstruction. The chosen labeling strategy targets: 1) Nephrin (podocyte slit diaphragm) to identify glomeruli and assess podocyte integrity; 2) Collagen IV (basement membrane) to outline glomerular tufts and measure volume; 3) IB4 lectin (endothelial glycocalyx) to highlight glomerular capillary loops; 4) DAPI for nuclear counterstain and segmentation. This combination allows precise glomerular identification, counting, volume measurement, and spatial mapping in cortex and medullary rays.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  **Delipidation and Decolorization**  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L solution (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N,N,N',N'-Tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine, 15 wt% Triton X-100 in Milli-Q water) on a shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
1.2 Replacement with fresh CUBIC-L solution and continued incubation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  

2  **Wash**  
2.1 Rinse with PBS-T (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) three times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3  **Immunolabeling**  
3.1 Blocking with PBS-T containing 5% normal donkey serum and 0.2% sodium azide. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-Nephrin (1:200), goat anti-Collagen IV (1:200), IB4-Alexa Fluor 555 (1:100), in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.3 Wash with PBS-T, three times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.5 Wash with PBS-T, three times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
3.6 Nuclear staining with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS-T). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.7 Final wash with PBS-T, three times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4  **Refractive Index Matching**  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ solution (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5% v/v N-methylnicotinamide in Milli-Q water, RI ~1.52) on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)  
4.2 Transfer to fresh CUBIC-R+ solution for final equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)  

5  **Mounting and Imaging**  
5.1 Mount the cleared kidney in CUBIC-R+ solution within a custom imaging chamber or glass-bottom dish. (Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)  
5.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 555, and Alexa Fluor 647.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing depth and tissue shrinkage minimization, which is critical for accurate volumetric analysis of glomeruli and their structures in a whole, fixed kidney. It provides excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-conjugated fluorescence, enabling robust multiplexed imaging of the two key slit diaphragm proteins (Nephrin and Podocin). The method is compatible with large, dense organs like the kidney. Lectin (IB4) is used to label the vasculature/glomerular endothelium as a structural reference, and Hoechst labels nuclei for segmentation. This combination allows for the simultaneous 3D assessment of slit diaphragm integrity, glomerular volume, and spatial context.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed kidney sample in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 20% (vol/vol) DMSO) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Wash sample in PBST (0.2% Triton X-100) for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2  Immunostaining and Labeling
2.1 Blocking with blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, and 10% (vol/vol) DMSO) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Primary antibody incubation: Incubate with a cocktail of chicken anti-Nephrin (1:200), rabbit anti-Podocin (1:200), and Isolectin GS-IB4 (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20, 5% DMSO, 3% donkey serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.3 Wash sample in PBST (0.2% Tween-20) for 24 hours, refreshing solution 4-6 times. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Secondary antibody and nuclear stain incubation: Incubate with donkey anti-chicken Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), and Hoechst 33342 (1:1000) in antibody dilution buffer. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.5 Final wash in PBST (0.2% Tween-20) for 24 hours, refreshing solution 4-6 times. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

3  Dehydration and Solvent Exchange
3.1 Gradual dehydration in a tert-butanol (tB) series: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% (vol/vol in H2O), each for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 84 hours total)
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) anhydrous tetrahydrofuran (THF) for 24 hours, refreshing once after 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4  Clearing and Refractive Index Matching
4.1 Incubation with clearing solution: Diphenyl ether (DPE) containing 0.5% (wt/vol) 2,2'-Thiodiethanol as an antioxidant. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24-48 hours, until optically clear)

The chosen labeling strategy uses a podocyte-specific marker (Podocin) to identify slit diaphragm-associated structures, while IB4 lectin directly labels the glomerular capillary lumen/vascular surface, enabling simultaneous 3D visualization of podocyte coverage and capillary architecture. 2.1 Rinse tissue 3 times with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
2.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-Podocin (NPHS2, 1:200) and biotinylated IB4 lectin (1:100) in blocking solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5–7 days)  
2.4 Wash 6 times with PBST, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and streptavidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5–7 days)  
2.6 Wash 6 times with PBST, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
2.7 Optional nuclear staining: Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.8 Final wash with PBST, 3 times for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3  **Refractive Index Matching & Clearing**  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ solution (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water, RI ~1.52) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1–2 days)  
3.2 Transfer to fresh CUBIC-R+ solution for final equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)  

4  **Mounting & Imaging**  
4.1 Mount the cleared kidney in CUBIC-R+ solution within an appropriate imaging chamber (e.g., glass-bottom dish or custom holder).  
4.2 Image using a light-sheet or confocal microscope equipped with 405 nm, 488 nm, and 640 nm laser lines.

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Nephrin (NPHS1)+Alexa Fluor 488, Podocin (NPHS2)+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS (Polyethylene glycol‑Associated Solvent System) is selected because it achieves excellent transparency in dense, lipid‑rich organs like kidney, with uniform clearing across cortex and medulla. It preserves endogenous fluorescence and antibody epitopes well, supports whole‑organ immunolabeling, and yields a high refractive index (RI ~1.52) compatible with high‑resolution deep imaging. The chosen markers directly address the scientific goals: Nephrin and Podocin are the two key slit‑diaphragm transmembrane proteins for assessing filtration barrier integrity; IB4‑lectin robustly labels glomerular endothelial/capillary boundaries for clear glomerular segmentation and volume measurement; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for tissue architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Tissue Preparation and Pre‑treatment  
1.1 Wash fixed kidney 3× with PBS, 30 min each, gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 in PBS for permeabilization. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Blocking and endogenous fluorescence quenching: Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X‑100, 0.01% sodium azide in PBS) containing 0.3 M glycine and 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium borohydride. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

2  Immunolabeling  
2.1 Primary antibody incubation: Incubation with chicken anti‑Nephrin (1:200), rabbit anti‑Podocin (1:200), and biotinylated IB4‑lectin (1:100) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
2.2 Wash 6× with PBS containing 0.1% Tween‑20 (PBST), 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Secondary antibody and streptavidin incubation: Incubation with donkey anti‑chicken Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
2.4 Wash 6× with PBST, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.5 Nuclear staining: Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.6 Final wash 3× with PBS, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

3  Dehydration and Lipid Removal  
3.1 Gradual dehydration: Sequential incubation in 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 95%, and 100% (vol/vol) tert‑butanol (t‑BuOH) in water, 4 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 28 hours)  
3.2 Delipidation: Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.3 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) t‑BuOH to remove residual DCM, 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate (BB) in t‑BuOH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) BB (RI ~1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Final RI adjustment: Incubation with BB:benzyl alcohol (BA) mixture (2:1 vol/vol, RI ~1.52). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5  Storage and Imaging  
5.1 Store cleared kidney in fresh BB:BA (2:1) solution in a light‑tight container. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: long‑term)  
5.2 Mount sample in imaging chamber filled with BB:BA (2:1) for light‑sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (UEA‑I)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous‑based clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence well and is highly effective for large, blood‑rich organs like the liver. It achieves excellent transparency and refractive‑index matching while maintaining the structural integrity of delicate ductal networks. CK19 is a specific marker for biliary epithelial cells, providing the primary signal for the entire bile duct tree. Lectin (UEA‑I) labels vascular endothelium, offering a reference map of portal tracts without interfering with the CK19 signal. DAPI stains nuclei, aiding in the identification of ductular reactions and cellular density in injury zones. The combination allows simultaneous 3D visualization of bile ducts, vasculature, and nuclei across whole liver lobes.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  **Delipidation and Decolorization**  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC‑L reagent (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N‑N‑dimethylformamide, 15 wt% Triton X‑100 in Milli‑Q water) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
1.2 Replacement with fresh CUBIC‑L reagent and continued incubation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  

2  **Wash**  
2.1 Rinse with PBS‑T (0.1% v/v Triton X‑100 in PBS) three times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3  **Immunolabeling**  
3.1 Blocking and permeabilization in PBS‑T containing 5% (v/v) normal goat serum and 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti‑CK19 (1:500) and biotinylated UEA‑I lectin (1:200) in PBS‑T with 1% serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.3 Wash with PBS‑T six times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: goat anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in PBS‑T with 1% serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.5 Wash with PBS‑T six times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
3.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS‑T. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.7 Final wash with PBS‑T three times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  

4  **Refractive‑Index Matching and Clearing**  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC‑R+ reagent (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5% v/v Triton X‑100 in Milli‑Q water, RI ≈ 1.52) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
4.2 Replacement with fresh CUBIC‑R+ reagent and continued incubation until the tissue is fully transparent. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2–3 days)  

5  **Mounting and Imaging**  
5.1 Transfer the cleared liver into a custom‑made imaging chamber filled with CUBIC‑R+ reagent. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)  
5.2 Secure the sample and perform light‑sheet or confocal microscopy using appropriate filter sets for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, and Alexa Fluor 647. (Temperature: RT, Time: as required)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [Anti-CK19 (胆管上皮标记), Anti-CK7 (胆管上皮标记), Lectin (凝集素, 血管腔面标记), DAPI (核标记)]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ 适用于已固定的完整器官（如小鼠肝脏），能有效去除血红素等内源性色素，显著降低背景自发荧光，这对于富含血液的肝脏样本至关重要。该方法通过甲醇系列脱水、双氧水漂白和有机溶剂透明化，能很好地保留荧光蛋白信号和抗体标记的荧光，兼容后续的免疫标记。选择CK19和CK7作为胆管上皮的特异性标记物，可交叉验证胆管网络结构。Lectin作为血管内皮标记，可提供门管区血管的参考坐标，帮助区分胆管与血管。DAPI用于勾勒细胞核位置，提供组织基本架构。

**Protocol Steps:**
1 脱水与漂白
1.1 梯度脱水：依次在20%、40%、60%、80%、100%、100%甲醇/PBS溶液（vol/vol）中孵育，每级1小时。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour each)
1.2 漂白：在含5% H2O2的20% DMSO/甲醇溶液中孵育。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2 再水化与通透
2.1 梯度再水化：依次在80%、60%、40%、20%甲醇/PBST溶液（0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS）中孵育，每级1小时。(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
2.2 洗涤：在PBST（0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS）中孵育。(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3 封闭与免疫标记
3.1 封闭：在含10%驴血清和0.2% Triton X-100的PBS溶液中孵育。(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.2 一抗孵育：在含3%驴血清、0.2% Triton X-100、0.1% NaN3的PBS溶液中，加入兔抗CK19抗体（1:500）和小鼠抗CK7抗体（1:500）进行孵育。(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
3.3 洗涤：在PBST（0.2% Tween-20 in PBS）中洗涤，每天更换3次溶液。(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CK19+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is selected because it is highly effective for clearing large, dense organs like the intact liver (20×15×10 mm), providing excellent transparency and minimal fluorescence quenching. Its aqueous-based delipidation and refractive index matching steps are gentle on epitopes, which is critical for preserving the signal of the key biliary marker CK19 and the vascular marker Lectin/IB4. The protocol allows for whole-organ immunolabeling prior to clearing, enabling deep penetration of antibodies and lectins to visualize the entire 3D biliary network and its spatial relationship with portal tracts. The use of CK19 (a canonical cholangiocyte marker) specifically highlights the biliary epithelium, while IB4 labels the vascular lumen to delineate portal vessels. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for structural context.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  **Sample Preparation & Permeabilization**  
1.1 Wash fixed liver in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) D‑sorbitol in PBST for 24 hours. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.3 Incubation with CUBIC‑L reagent (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N‑N‑diethylenetriamine, 15 wt% Triton X‑100 in water) for 7 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

2  **Immunolabeling & Lectin Staining**  
2.1 Wash in PBST for 24 hours, refreshing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 1% (wt/vol) BSA, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 in PBS for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti‑CK19 (1:500) and biotinylated IB4 (1:200) in blocking solution for 14 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 14 days)  
2.4 Wash in PBST for 48 hours, refreshing solution every 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: goat anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution for 10 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 10 days)  
2.6 Wash in PBST for 48 hours, refreshing solution every 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
2.7 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.8 Wash in PBS for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3  **Delipidation & Decolorization**  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC‑L reagent for 7 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

4  **Refractive Index Matching**  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC‑R+ reagent (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide in water, RI ≈ 1.52) for 7 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: 7 days)  

5  **Mounting & Imaging**  
5.1 Transfer cleared liver to a custom imaging chamber filled with fresh CUBIC‑R+. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
5.2 Image using light‑sheet or confocal microscope with appropriate filter sets for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, and Alexa Fluor 647.

请根据该科学问题选择兼容的荧光/标记策略，并选择匹配的组织透明方法。若直接 F-actin 探针只能显示气道壁骨架结构，不能替代平滑肌身份标记；若需要追踪肺内神经分布，则应选择给定标记物列表中的肺部神经相关靶点。请仅输出 protocol，第 1 行写明所选荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-SMA+Alexa Fluor 488, Hu C/D+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency and strong tissue shrinkage (up to ~65% volume reduction), which is advantageous for imaging a relatively large, dense organ like the lung. It preserves fluorescence of antibody-conjugated dyes (e.g., Alexa Fluor) exceptionally well over long periods and is compatible with whole-mount immunolabeling. The shrinkage also improves imaging speed and resolution for detailed 3D reconstruction of airway smooth muscle and neural architecture. The labeling strategy uses alpha-SMA (smooth muscle actin) to specifically mark airway smooth muscle layer (not just F-actin cytoskeleton), and Hu C/D (PGP9.5) as a pan-neuronal marker to label pulmonary vagal nerve fibers. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for structural orientation.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Whole-Mount Immunolabeling (Post-Fixation)
1.1 Wash fixed lung lobes in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours, changing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.2 Block and permeabilize in PBST containing 5% normal donkey serum and 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-alpha-SMA (1:200) and mouse anti-Hu C/D (PGP9.5, 1:200) in PBST with 3% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.4 Wash in PBST for 24 hours, changing solution every 6 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBST with 3% normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.6 Wash in PBST for 24 hours, changing solution every 6 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.7 Incubate with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.8 Wash in PBS for 6 hours, changing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

2  Dehydration
2.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

3  Delipidation and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)

4  Refractive Index Matching
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, until tissue is transparent)

5  Storage and Imaging
5.1 Store cleared lung lobes in fresh DBE in a light-tight container at 4 ℃ until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: long-term)
5.2 Mount sample in DBE-filled imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS (Revised Protocol)
**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA+Alexa Fluor 488, SM22α+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]
**Justification:** The original PEGASOS method is retained but critically revised to address the stated issues. PEGASOS is highly suitable for large, dense organs like lungs, offering excellent decalcification/delipidation and refractive index matching for deep imaging. The revisions (extended delipidation, mandatory decoloration, and optimized RI matching) directly target the problems of weak signal and uneven clearing. The chosen labeling strategy uses two canonical smooth muscle markers (α-SMA for mature myofibroblasts/smooth muscle, SM22α for differentiated smooth muscle) for dual-channel assessment. Lectin (IB4) is added to outline airway/vascular lumens and neural structures (including vagal endings), providing essential anatomical context without introducing extra targets. DAPI labels nuclei for cellular reference. All fluorophores (Alexa Fluor series) are compatible with PEGASOS and provide bright, photostable signals.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Decalcification & Decoloration (Critical for Blood Removal and Uniform Clearing)
1.1 Incubation with Decalcification Solution (10% w/v EDTA in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4) on a shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.2 Wash with 0.1 M PBS (pH 7.4) three times, 1 hour each, on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

1.4 Wash with 0.1 M PBS (pH 7.4) three times, 1 hour each, on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

2  Immunostaining & Lectin Labeling (Performed on Whole Lobe)
2.1 Permeabilization and Blocking: Incubation with Permeabilization/Blocking Buffer (0.5% v/v Triton X-100, 5% v/v normal donkey serum, 1% w/v BSA in 0.1 M PBS) on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

2.5 Wash: Wash with Wash Buffer six times, 2 hours each, on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)
2.6 Nuclear Staining: Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in 0.1 M PBS) on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.7 Final Wash: Wash with 0.1 M PBS three times, 1 hour each, on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

3  Delipidation & Dehydration (Extended for Uniform Clearing)
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in ddH2O on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

3.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
3.7 Incubation with 33% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.8 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Insulin+Alexa Fluor 488, Glucagon+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based clearing method that is highly effective for soft, irregular organs like the pancreas, providing excellent transparency and minimal tissue deformation. It preserves endogenous fluorescence and antibody labeling well, which is critical for long-term imaging of large samples. The protocol is scalable and compatible with whole-organ processing. For the scientific goal of quantifying all β-cells and islets in 3D, direct immunolabeling of Insulin (β-cells) and Glucagon (α-cells) is essential; DAPI provides nuclear reference for cell density and islet delineation. Alexa Fluor dyes are photostable and compatible with CUBIC’s refractive index matching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  **Delipidation and Decolorization**  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L reagent (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% Quadrol, 15 wt% Triton X-100 in water) on a shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
1.2 Replacement with fresh CUBIC-L reagent and continued incubation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 days)  

2  **Wash**  
2.1 Rinse with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) three times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3  **Immunolabeling**  
3.1 Blocking and permeabilization with PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: guinea pig anti-Insulin (1:500) and mouse anti-Glucagon (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.3 Wash with PBST, changing solution every 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-guinea pig Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.5 Wash with PBST, changing solution every 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total)  
3.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.7 Final wash with PBST, three times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4  **Refractive Index Matching**  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ reagent (45 wt% sucrose, 30 wt% urea, 10 wt% 2,2',2''-nitrilotriethanol in water, RI ≈ 1.48) on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)  
4.2 Transfer to fresh CUBIC-R+ reagent for final equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)  

5  **Mounting and Imaging**  
5.1 Place sample in imaging chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ reagent. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
5.2 Image using light-sheet or confocal microscope with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 647, and DAPI.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Insulin+Alexa Fluor 488, PDX1+Alexa Fluor 647, Nkx6.1+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and antibody epitopes exceptionally well, which is critical for multiplexed detection of hormones (Insulin) and transcription factors (PDX1, Nkx6.1) in a delicate organ like the pancreas. It provides homogeneous clearing for whole organs up to ~1 cm³, matching the mouse pancreas size. The refractive index (RI) can be adjusted to ~1.52 for high-resolution 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). DAPI is included as a nuclear counterstain to help define islet boundaries and cell nuclei.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  **Delipidation & Decolorization (CUBIC-L)**  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L reagent (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% Quadrol, 15 wt% Triton X-100 in distilled water) on a gentle shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
1.2 Replacement with fresh CUBIC-L reagent and continued incubation. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days)  
1.3 Rinse with PBS-T (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) for 1 hour to remove residual CUBIC-L. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

2  **Immunolabeling**  
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization with PBS-T containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: Guinea pig anti-Insulin (1:500), Rabbit anti-PDX1 (1:300), Mouse anti-Nkx6.1 (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
2.3 Wash with PBS-T, changing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Donkey anti-Guinea Pig Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), Donkey anti-Mouse Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
2.5 Wash with PBS-T, changing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  
2.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.7 Final wash with PBS-T. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3  **Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC-R+)**  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ reagent (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide, 0.5% wt/vol N‑N‑diethylamino propylamine in distilled water, RI ~1.52) on a gentle shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)  
3.2 Transfer to fresh CUBIC-R+ reagent for final equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 day)

4  **Mounting & Imaging**  
4.1 Mount the cleared pancreas in a chamber filled with CUBIC-R+ reagent.  
4.2 Image using a light-sheet or confocal microscope equipped with appropriate lasers/filters for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, 555, and 647.

The protocol includes a delipidation step that simultaneously decolorizes heme, which is beneficial for the blood‑rich pancreas. The chosen labeling strategy directly targets the scientific goals: Insulin (β‑cell hormone product), PDX1 (key β‑cell transcription factor), and Glucagon (α‑cell marker for islet identification). DAPI serves as a nuclear counterstain for structural reference. The overlap of Insulin and PDX1 signals increases the reliability of β‑cell quantification.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  **Delipidation & Decolorization (CUBIC‑R1)**  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC‑R1 solution (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% Quadrol, 15 wt% Triton X‑100 in distilled water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
1.2 Replacement with fresh CUBIC‑R1 solution. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)  

2  **Wash**  
2.1 Rinse with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 (PBST) three times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3  **Immunolabeling**  
3.1 Blocking and permeabilization in PBST with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: guinea pig anti‑Insulin (1:500), rabbit anti‑PDX1 (1:300), mouse anti‑Glucagon (1:300) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.3 Wash with PBST six times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti‑guinea pig Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti‑mouse Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)

3.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.7 Wash with PBST three times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4  **Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC‑R2)**  
4.1 Incubation with CUBIC‑R2 solution (50 wt% sucrose, 25 wt% urea, 10 wt% 2,2',2''‑nitrilotriethanol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 in distilled water, RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)

5.1 Mount the cleared pancreas in a chamber filled with CUBIC‑R2 solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Insulin+Alexa Fluor 488, PDX1+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency with minimal tissue shrinkage and deformation, crucial for preserving the delicate architecture of intact pancreatic islets. It offers excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-derived fluorescence, which is essential for detecting both β-cell hormone (Insulin) and transcription factor (PDX1) signals. The method is faster than the prolonged CUBIC delipidation that caused structural damage and signal loss, and it is compatible with whole-organ 3D quantitative imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)  
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

2  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, repeat until tissue is transparent)  

3  Immunostaining (Performed after Step 1.4, before Step 1.5)  
3.1 Permeabilization and blocking in PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, and 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: guinea pig anti-Insulin (1:500) and rabbit anti-PDX1 (1:300) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with 3 solution changes)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-guinea pig Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with 3 solution changes)  
3.6 Nuclear counterstain with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.7 Wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, with 2 solution changes)  
3.8 Resume dehydration starting at Step 1.4 (100% methanol)  

4  Storage and Imaging  
4.1 Store cleared pancreas in fresh dibenzyl ether (DBE) in a light-tight container (Temperature: RT, Indefinitely)  
4.2 For imaging, mount sample in DBE within an appropriate imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (Tyrosine Hydroxylase) + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it is highly effective for clearing large, lipid-rich tissues (like white adipose tissue) by combining dehydration with organic-solvent-based delipidation and RI matching, resulting in excellent transparency and minimal tissue shrinkage/expansion. It preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes exceptionally well over long periods. TH (Tyrosine Hydroxylase) is the definitive marker for sympathetic noradrenergic fibers. Lectin (IB4) labels vasculature, providing a spatial reference for perivascular nerve fibers. DAPI labels nuclei to define tissue architecture and fat lobules. This combination allows 3D mapping of sympathetic nerve fibers (TH⁺) relative to blood vessels (Lectin⁺) and tissue compartments.

    1.2 Incubate in permeabilization solution (PBS with 0.5% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine) for 24 hours at 37°C on a shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2  **Immunolabeling & Counterstaining**
    2.1 Block in blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 6% normal donkey serum) for 24 hours at 37°C on a shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
    2.2 Incubate with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-Tyrosine Hydroxylase (1:500) and biotinylated IB4 Lectin (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20, 5% DMSO, 3% donkey serum) for 72 hours at 37°C on a shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
    2.3 Wash with PBST (0.2% Tween-20) 6 times, 2 hours each, at 37°C on a shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours total)
    2.4 Incubate with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer for 72 hours at 37°C on a shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
    2.5 Wash with PBST (0.2% Tween-20) 6 times, 2 hours each, at 37°C on a shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours total)
    2.6 Incubate with DAPI (5 µg/mL) in PBS for 24 hours at 37°C on a shaker. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

3  **Dehydration & Delipidation (uDISCO Clearing)**
    3.1 Dehydrate in a graded tert-butanol (tB) series: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% tB (vol/vol in H₂O), each step for 4 hours at RT on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 28 hours total)
    3.2 Incubate in 100% anhydrous tetrahydrofuran (THF) for 12 hours at RT on a shaker. Replace with fresh 100% THF and incubate for another 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)
    3.3 Incubate in fresh 100% THF for an additional 12 hours at RT on a shaker to ensure complete dehydration and delipidation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4  **Refractive Index Matching & Storage**
    4.1 Incubate in uDISCO clearing solution: 85.6 vol% dibenzyl ether (DBE) with 14.4 vol% diphenyl sulfide (DPS) (RI ~1.56) for 12 hours at RT without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
    4.2 Transfer cleared tissue to fresh uDISCO solution (DBE:DPS) for long-term storage and imaging. Store in the dark at 4°C. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite)
