**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH (Tyrosine Hydroxylase) + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency in large, lipid-rich tissues (like intact WAT pads) while strongly preserving endogenous and antibody-derived fluorescence over long periods. Its organic-solvent-based delipidation efficiently removes fat, which is critical for clearing adipose tissue, and the final refractive index (RI ~1.56) is ideal for high-resolution deep-tissue 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). The labeling strategy uses TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) as a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers, IB4 lectin to label vascular endothelial luminal surfaces (providing a clear vascular network reference), and DAPI for nuclear counterstaining to delineate tissue regions. This combination allows precise 3D mapping of nerve-vessel spatial relationships.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  **Sample Preparation & Permeabilization**
1.1 Wash fixed tissue (15 mm × 10 mm × 5 mm) in PBS, 3 × 1 hour, with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)
1.2 Incubation in permeabilization solution: PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 20% (vol/vol) DMSO. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

2  **Immunolabeling & Lectin Staining**
2.1 Blocking in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, and 6% (wt/vol) BSA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Primary antibody incubation: Anti-Tyrosine Hydroxylase (rabbit polyclonal, 1:500) and IB4-biotin conjugate (20 µg/mL) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.3 Wash in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 3 × 2 hours, then 3 × 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 42 hours total)
2.4 Secondary antibody/streptavidin incubation: Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.5 Wash in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 3 × 2 hours, then 3 × 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 42 hours total)
2.6 Nuclear counterstain: Incubation in PBS with 1 µg/mL DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.7 Final wash in PBS, 3 × 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

3  **Dehydration & Delipidation**
3.1 Gradual dehydration in methanol/water series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol, each step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per step)
3.2 Incubation in 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.3 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) DCM, 2 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)

4  **Refractive Index Matching & Clearing**
4.1 Incubation in dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) until tissue is fully transparent (RI ~1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24-48 hours, monitor clarity)

5  **Storage & Imaging**
5.1 Store cleared sample in fresh DBE in a light-tight container at 4 ℃ until imaging.
5.2 For imaging, mount sample in DBE within an appropriate chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647 conjugate), IB4 (Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate), DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO provides exceptional tissue shrinkage and hardening, which is crucial for maintaining the structural integrity of the delicate, blood-filled placental vasculature during clearing and handling. Its high refractive index (RI ~1.56) enables high-resolution imaging of dense vascular networks. The protocol's dehydration steps effectively remove water and lipids, reducing light scattering from lipid-rich membranes and residual blood components (hemoglobin), which addresses the problem of high background. Lectin (e.g., UEA-I, LEA) and IB4 selectively bind to glycocalyx on vascular endothelial cells, providing strong, specific labeling of the perfused vascular lumen and endothelial surface, ideal for 3D reconstruction of branching structures. DAPI counterstains nuclei, aiding in defining tissue architecture and identifying avascular regions.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)

2  Fluorescent Labeling
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary labeling solution (Lectin-Alexa Fluor 647 at 5 µg/mL, IB4-Alexa Fluor 488 at 10 µg/mL, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48-72 hours with gentle agitation)
2.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated four times)
2.4 Incubation with nuclear counterstain solution (DAPI at 1 µg/mL in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.5 Final wash with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes, repeated three times)

3  Dehydration for Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)

4  uDISCO Clearing and RI Matching
4.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Benzyl Ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: Until tissue is fully transparent and sinks, typically 12-24 hours)
4.4 Storage and imaging in fresh 100% (vol/vol) Benzyl Ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinitely)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its excellent clearing of whole organs (including placenta), strong fluorescence preservation for Alexa Fluor dyes, and compatibility with immunolabeling. The method achieves high transparency and refractive index matching suitable for high-resolution 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). The labeling strategy uses CD31 (PECAM1) to mark all endothelial structures (morphological vasculature) and fluorescently labeled Lectin (IB4) injected intravascularly to label perfused functional luminal surfaces. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for tissue architecture. This dual-channel approach directly addresses the goal of distinguishing "endothelial-lined vessels" from "functionally perfused vessels."

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  **Sample Preparation and Permeabilization**  
1.1 Wash fixed placenta (10 mm × 8 mm × 3 mm) in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
1.2 Incubation in permeabilization solution (PBS with 0.5% Triton X-100, 20% DMSO, 0.3 M glycine) without shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2  **Blocking and Immunolabeling**  
2.1 Incubation in blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 6% normal donkey serum). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody rat anti-mouse CD31 (1:200 in PBS with 0.2% Tween-20, 5% DMSO, 3% donkey serum) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash in PBST with 0.1% Tween-20, refreshing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500 in PBS with 0.2% Tween-20, 3% donkey serum) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash in PBST with 0.1% Tween-20, refreshing solution every 8 hours. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

3  **Nuclear Staining and Lectin Perfusion Labeling (Functional Channel)**  
3.1 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in PBS) without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash in PBS to remove excess DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
*Note: Intravascular perfusion of fluorescent Lectin (IB4-Alexa Fluor 488) must be performed in vivo prior to tissue fixation. After fixation, the signal is preserved and no further in vitro labeling is needed.*  

4  **Dehydration and Delipidation**  
4.1 Gradual dehydration in methanol/water series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol (each step in fresh solution). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per step)  
4.2 Incubation in fresh 100% methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Incubation in 66% dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% methanol (vol/vol). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.4 Incubation in 100% DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)  

5  **Refractive Index Matching and Clearing**  
5.1 Incubation in dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) until tissue is fully transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours)  
5.2 Store cleared sample in fresh DBE for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: long-term storage)

**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647 conjugate), IB4 (Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate), CD31 (Alexa Fluor 750 conjugate)]
**Justification:** uDISCO provides exceptional tissue shrinkage and hardening, which is advantageous for handling and imaging a delicate, fixed whole placenta. The chosen labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goal: Lectin and IB4 bind to glycocalyx components on perfused vascular luminal surfaces, serving as primary markers for functional, perfused vessels. CD31 (PECAM-1) is added as a pan-endothelial marker to provide a complete structural reference of the entire vascular network, enabling the identification of non-perfused, sparse, or abnormally dilated vessels through signal comparison.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Labeling
1.1 Wash fixed placenta sample in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, with 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

1.4 Wash sample in PBST on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with solution change every 2 hours)
1.5 Incubation in secondary antibody and lectin cocktail: Donkey anti-Rat IgG Alexa Fluor 750 (1:500), IB4-Alexa Fluor 488 (10 µg/mL), and Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum)-Alexa Fluor 647 (20 µg/mL) in blocking solution on a shaker. Protect from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
1.6 Wash sample in PBST on a shaker, protected from light. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, with solution change every 3 hours)
2  Dehydration
2.1 Incubation in 30% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation in 50% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it provides excellent whole-organ transparency, strong fluorescence preservation (especially for Alexa Fluor dyes), and effectively clears blood-rich tissues via its tert-butanol dehydration and decolorization steps. The method is optimized for deep antibody penetration in intact organs (~1 cm scale) and yields a high refractive index (RI ~1.56) suitable for high-resolution light-sheet imaging of 3D vascular networks. Using CD31 (endothelial marker) plus Lectin (IB4, which binds vascular glycocalyx and luminal surfaces) allows simultaneous structural and functional perfusion-surface labeling. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain. The protocol includes extended incubation times to ensure uniform labeling throughout the dense placental core.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Decolorization
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)
1.5 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2  Delipidation and Bleaching
2.1 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
2.2 Incubation with 100% tert-butanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.3 Incubation with fresh 100% tert-butanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3  Rehydration and Permeabilization
3.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) tert-butanol in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) tert-butanol in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.7 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 3 times)
3.8 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.1% Tween-20, 10% DMSO).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4  Immunostaining and Lectin Labeling
4.1 Blocking with blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.1% Tween-20, 10% DMSO, 6% normal donkey serum).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rat anti-CD31 (1:200) and biotinylated IB4 Lectin (1:100) in antibody solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.1% Tween-20, 5% DMSO, 3% normal donkey serum).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)
4.3 Wash with wash buffer (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.1% Tween-20).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, buffer changed every 8 hours)
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in antibody solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)
4.5 Wash with wash buffer.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, buffer changed every 8 hours)
4.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.7 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, buffer changed every 4 hours)

5  Final Dehydration and Clearing
5.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.4 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
5.5 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
5.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
5.7 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeat twice)
5.8 Incubation with 100% tert-butanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
5.9 Incubation with fresh 100% tert-butanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6  Refractive Index Matching
6.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution: 85% (vol/vol) tert-butanol, 15% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate, with 0.4% (vol/vol) diphenyl ether (RI ~1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours until fully transparent)
6.2 Storage in fresh uDISCO clearing solution at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488 (生殖细胞特异性 RNA 解旋酶), Alexa Fluor 647 (减数分裂联会复合体蛋白)]  
**Justification:** CUBIC 是一种水基、温和的透明化方法，能很好地保留荧光蛋白和抗体标记的荧光信号，尤其适合中等尺寸的软组织（如小鼠睾丸）。它通过去垢剂和尿素实现高效脱脂，同时保持蛋白质抗原性，有利于多重免疫标记。DAPI 作为核染料可辅助判断细胞层次和核形态；Alexa Fluor 488 和 Alexa Fluor 647 分别标记生殖细胞特异性 RNA 解旋酶和减数分裂联会复合体蛋白，可实现双通道特异性识别，满足对生殖细胞总体分布和精母细胞阶段定位的科学目标。  

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 组织预处理与通透  
1.1 将固定后的小鼠睾丸（约 8 mm × 5 mm × 4 mm）置于 PBS 中漂洗 3 次，每次 1 小时。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.2 通透处理：将样本浸入含 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 的 PBS 溶液中。(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 免疫标记  
2.1 封闭：将样本转移至含 5% (wt/vol) BSA 和 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 的 PBS 封闭液中。(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 一抗孵育：将样本浸入含抗生殖细胞特异性 RNA 解旋酶抗体（1:200）和抗减数分裂联会复合体蛋白抗体（1:200）的封闭液中。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 洗涤：用含 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 的 PBS 洗涤样本 6 次，每次 2 小时。(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.4 二抗孵育：将样本浸入含 Alexa Fluor 488 偶联二抗（1:500）和 Alexa Fluor 647 偶联二抗（1:500）的封闭液中。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 洗涤：重复步骤 2.3 的洗涤过程。(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 核染色  
3.1 将样本浸入含 1 µg/mL DAPI 的 PBS 溶液中。(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 用 PBS 洗涤样本 3 次，每次 1 小时。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

4 脱色与脱脂（CUBIC 试剂 R1）  
4.1 将样本浸入 CUBIC-R1 试剂（25 wt% 尿素，25 wt% N,N,N',N'-四（2-羟丙基）乙二胺，15 wt% 曲拉通 X-100）。(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
4.2 更换新鲜 CUBIC-R1 试剂，继续孵育。(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

5 折射率匹配（CUBIC 试剂 R2）  
5.1 将样本转移至 CUBIC-R2 试剂（50 wt% 蔗糖，25 wt% 尿素，10 wt% 2,2',2''-次氮基三乙醇，0.1% vol/vol Triton X-100）。(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.2 更换新鲜 CUBIC-R2 试剂，继续孵育直至组织完全透明（通常需 24-48 小时）。(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

6 成像前处理  
6.1 将透明化样本置于折射率匹配的成像腔中，浸没于 CUBIC-R2 试剂中。(Temperature: RT, Time: 立即成像)  
6.2 建议使用光片显微镜进行三维成像，激发波长分别为 405 nm (DAPI)、488 nm (Alexa Fluor 488) 和 640 nm (Alexa Fluor 647)。

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DAPI, Hoechst, TO-PRO-3, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)-Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its ability to rapidly clear and shrink large, dense organs (like the fixed whole mouse testis) while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody signals. The method achieves high transparency and significant sample size reduction, facilitating high-resolution 3D imaging of the entire seminiferous tubule network. The chosen nuclear dyes (DAPI/Hoechst/TO-PRO-3) provide dense, pan-nuclear labeling to delineate all cell layers and identify nuclear morphology patterns characteristic of spermatogonia, spermatocytes, and spermatids. Phalloidin labels F-actin in the cytoskeleton, highlighting tubular architecture and cellular outlines. Lectin IB4 binds to glycans on the basement membrane and vasculature, outlining the tubule boundaries and interstitial spaces. This multi-channel strategy allows for simultaneous mapping of nuclear stratification, tubular morphology, and interstitial landmarks, enabling the 3D reconstruction of the spermatogenic wave and cellular hierarchy within intact tubules.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour, repeated twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM for 15 minutes, repeated twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes total)  

2  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
2.2 Replacement with fresh 100% DBE and incubation until the sample is fully transparent (typically 12-24 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12-24 hours)  

3  Staining (Integrated before Step 1 if performing immunolabeling; for direct dye staining, perform after Step 1.5)  
3.1  Blocking and Permeabilization (if performing antibody staining)  
3.1.1 Incubation with permeabilization solution (0.2% Triton X-100, 10% DMSO, 20% normal goat serum in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.1.2 Incubation with primary antibody (e.g., anti-β-III Tubulin for spermatid tails, 1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% DMSO, 10% normal goat serum in PBS) for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
3.1.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBS-T) for 12 hours, with 3-4 solution changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (e.g., Alexa Fluor 568, 1:500) in antibody dilution buffer for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.1.5 Wash with PBS-T for 12 hours, with 3-4 solution changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3.2  Direct Dye Staining (can be combined with or performed instead of antibody staining)  
3.2.1 Incubation with nuclear dye cocktail (1 µg/mL DAPI, 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342, 1 µM TO-PRO-3) in PBS for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2.2 Incubation with phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200) and Lectin IB4-Alexa Fluor 488 (10 µg/mL) in PBS for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.2.3 Wash with PBS for 12 hours, with 3-4 solution changes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4  Final Clearing and Storage  
4.1 After staining and washing, resume dehydration from Step 1.5 (100% methanol) through Step 2.2.  
4.2 Store the cleared sample in fresh 100% DBE at 4 ℃ in the dark until imaging. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)  

5  Imaging Preparation  
5.1 Mount the cleared testis in a custom imaging chamber filled with 100% DBE.  
5.2 Perform light-sheet or confocal microscopy using appropriate filter sets for DAPI/Hoechst (blue), Alexa Fluor 488 (green), Alexa Fluor 568 (red, if used), TO-PRO-3/Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (far-red).

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Hu C/D (PGP9.5) + Alexa Fluor 647, Neurofilament-L (Pan-neuronal fiber) + Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its excellent clearing depth and high transparency in large, dense tissues (like the 6 cm colon), strong preservation of endogenous and antibody-derived fluorescence, and compatibility with whole-mount immunolabeling. Its organic-solvent-based dehydration and delipidation efficiently clear the lipid-rich intestinal wall while maintaining structural integrity. The labeling strategy uses Hu C/D (PGP9.5) as a pan-neuronal cytoplasmic marker for neuronal somata in both plexuses, Neurofilament-L for pan-neuronal fibers, Hoechst for nuclei to aid in cell density assessment, and Phalloidin to delineate the muscular layers and tissue architecture, providing essential spatial context for plexus localization and regional comparisons.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  **Dehydration and Permeabilization**
    1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
    1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
    1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
    1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
    1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)

2  **Delipidation and Bleaching (Optional)**
    2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

3  **Rehydration and Blocking**
    3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
    3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
    3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
    3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
    3.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBS-T). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated three times)
    3.6 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 10 µg/ml anti-CD16/32). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4  **Primary Antibody Staining**
    4.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in blocking solution: Rabbit anti-Hu C/D (PGP9.5, 1:500), Chicken anti-Neurofilament-L (1:500). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)

5  **Washing**
    5.1 Wash with PBS-T. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours, repeated six times)

6  **Secondary Antibody and Dye Staining**
    6.1 Incubation with secondary antibody and dye cocktail in blocking solution: Donkey anti-Rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), Donkey anti-Chicken IgG Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500), Hoechst 33342 (1:1000), Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)

7  **Washing and Final Dehydration**
    7.1 Wash with PBS-T. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours, repeated six times)
    7.2 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
    7.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
    7.4 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
    7.5 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
    7.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)

8  **Clearing and Refractive Index Matching**
    8.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
    8.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
    8.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ~1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, repeated once until tissue is fully transparent)

9  **Storage and Imaging**
    9.1 Store cleared tissue in fresh 100% DBE in a light-tight container at RT until imaging. Mount in DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** EyeCi  
**Chosen Labeling:** [IB4-Alexa Fluor 647, NeuN-Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** EyeCi is specifically optimized for whole-eye clearing, effectively removing pigments (including RPE melanin) while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody/lectin labeling. It maintains tissue integrity and is compatible with subsequent immunolabeling. IB4 directly labels retinal vasculature. NeuN is a well-established nuclear marker for retinal ganglion cells (RGCs). DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for overall cytoarchitecture. This combination allows simultaneous 3D visualization of RGCs, vasculature, and retinal layers in the intact globe.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  **Delipidation and Decolorization**
    1.1 Incubation with EyeCi solution A (25 wt% urea, 0.1% w/v Triton X-100 in 0.1 M PB, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
    1.2 Incubation with EyeCi solution B (25 wt% urea, 0.1% w/v Triton X-100, 20 wt% N-methylacetamide in 0.1 M PB, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
    1.3 Incubation with EyeCi solution C (25 wt% urea, 0.1% w/v Triton X-100, 50 wt% N-methylacetamide in 0.1 M PB, pH 7.4).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2  **Immunolabeling and Lectin Staining**
    2.1 Wash with 0.1 M PB containing 0.1% w/v Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours with 3 solution changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
    2.2 Blocking and permeabilization with 5% v/v normal donkey serum, 1% w/v BSA, 0.5% v/v Triton X-100 in 0.1 M PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
    2.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: mouse anti-NeuN (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
    2.4 Wash with PBST for 24 hours with 6 solution changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
    2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody and lectin cocktail: donkey anti-mouse IgG-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and IB4-Alexa Fluor 647 (20 µg/mL) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
    2.6 Wash with PBST for 24 hours with 6 solution changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
    2.7 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in 0.1 M PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
    2.8 Wash with 0.1 M PB for 12 hours with 4 solution changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3  **Refractive Index Matching**
    3.1 Incubation with EyeCi solution D (88% v/v Histodenz in 0.1 M PB, RI = 1.46).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
    3.2 Incubation with EyeCi solution E (97% v/v Histodenz in 0.1 M PB, RI = 1.48).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4  **Mounting and Storage**
    4.1 Transfer cleared and labeled eye to a glass-bottom imaging dish filled with EyeCi solution E.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)
    4.2 Seal dish with parafilm and store in the dark at 4 ℃ until imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: long-term)

**Chosen Method:** EyeCi  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, Hu C/D (PGP9.5) + Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** EyeCi is specifically optimized for whole-eye clearing, preserving delicate retinal architecture and endogenous fluorescence while achieving high transparency for a 3–4 mm fixed mouse eyeball. It maintains epitope integrity for multiple antibody labeling. The chosen markers allow cross‑validation: NeuN labels mature retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), Hu C/D labels all neuronal populations including RGCs, and DAPI provides nuclear reference. Using two distinct RGC identity markers (NeuN and Hu C/D) with spectrally separated fluorophores enables direct comparison of overlap, regional distribution, and cell‑count consistency, reducing false‑negatives from single‑marker approaches.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  **Sample Preparation**  
1.1 Post‑fixation in 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS for 2 hours at 4 ℃. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 (PBST) 3 times, 30 min each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours)  

2  **Immunolabeling**  
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization in PBST with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti‑NeuN (1:500) and anti‑Hu C/D (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBST 6 times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti‑mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST 6 times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.7 Final wash with PBS 3 times, 30 min each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours)  

3  **EyeCi Clearing**  
3.1 Dehydration in graded methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in water, each for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours)  
3.2 Delipidation in 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.3 Wash in 100% (vol/vol) methanol twice, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.4 Refractive‑index matching in EyeCi solution (88% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate, RI = 1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4  **Mounting and Imaging**  
4.1 Transfer cleared eyeball into a glass‑bottom imaging dish filled with fresh EyeCi solution.  
4.2 Image using light‑sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, and Alexa Fluor 647.

**Chosen Method:** EyeCi  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647 conjugate), NeuN (Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate), DAPI]  
**Justification:** EyeCi is specifically optimized for clearing intact mouse eyes, preserving both tissue morphology and endogenous fluorescence. It provides excellent transparency for the entire globe (~3–4 mm) while maintaining structural integrity, which is critical for mapping 3D spatial relationships between retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and the superficial vascular plexus. The method is relatively rapid and compatible with antibody and lectin labeling. Lectin (e.g., Isolectin B4, IB4) directly labels endothelial cells for vascular mapping, while an anti-NeuN antibody reliably labels RGC nuclei. DAPI provides a general nuclear counterstain for orientation.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed whole mouse eye twice with 1x PBS, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution: 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 20% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
1.3 Wash with PBST three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

2  Immunostaining and Lectin Labeling
2.1 Blocking with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Primary antibody incubation: Anti-NeuN (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBST six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)
2.4 Secondary antibody and lectin incubation: Donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated Lectin (IB4, 1:100) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBST six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)
2.6 Nuclear counterstain: Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.7 Final wash with PBST three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

3  Dehydration and Delipidation
3.1 Gradual dehydration in methanol/PBS series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in deionized water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each step)
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated twice)
3.3 Delipidation: Incubation with EyeCi delipidation solution (33% (vol/vol) Quadrol, 40% (vol/vol) N‑methyl‑D‑glucamine in methanol). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
4.1 Wash with EyeCi washing solution (40% (wt/vol) N‑methyl‑D‑glucamine in deionized water). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated twice)
4.2 Refractive index matching: Incubation with EyeCi clearing solution (40% (wt/vol) N‑methyl‑D‑glucamine, 40% (wt/vol) Histodenz in deionized water, RI ~1.46). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5  Mounting and Storage
5.1 Transfer cleared eye to fresh EyeCi clearing solution in an imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)
5.2 For long-term storage, seal the chamber and store at 4 ℃ in the dark.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [IB4 (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, Hu C/D+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS (Polyethylene glycol‑Associated Solvent System) is selected because it effectively removes pigments (including RPE melanin) and lipids through strong organic solvent-based decolorization and delipidation, which directly addresses the problem of strong RPE background and light absorption. Its multi-step dehydration and bleaching protocol is well-suited for dense, pigmented tissues like the whole mouse eye. The final RI matching solution (BB-PEGASOS) provides high transparency and is compatible with long-term storage and high-resolution 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). The labeling strategy uses IB4 (lectin) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 to robustly label the entire retinal vasculature (including endothelial surface), Hu C/D (a pan-neuronal marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 to identify retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), and DAPI for nuclear counterstaining to define retinal layers. All chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI) are compatible with the organic solvent steps of PEGASOS and provide strong, photostable signals for dual-channel detection and 3D analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  **Sample Preparation and Pre-treatment**
    1.1  Wash fixed whole mouse eye (3–4 mm diameter) in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, 3 times for 30 minutes each on a gentle shaker. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1.5 hours total)
    1.2  Permeabilization and blocking: Incubate sample in PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide, and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours on a gentle shaker)

2  **Immunolabeling and Vascular Staining**
    2.1  Primary antibody incubation: Incubate sample in blocking solution containing rabbit anti-Hu C/D (1:500) and biotinylated IB4 lectin (20 µg/mL). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days on a gentle shaker)
    2.2  Wash: Rinse sample with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide (PBS-TA), 4 times for 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours total)
    2.3  Secondary antibody and streptavidin incubation: Incubate sample in blocking solution containing donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days on a gentle shaker)
    2.4  Wash: Rinse sample with PBS-TA, 4 times for 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 8 hours total)
    2.5  Nuclear staining: Incubate sample in PBS containing 1 µg/mL DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours on a gentle shaker)
    2.6  Final wash: Rinse sample with PBS, 3 times for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

3  **Dehydration and Decolorization (PEGASOS Bleaching)**
    3.1  Dehydration: Incubate sample in a graded series of tert-butanol (tB) in distilled water: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% (vol/vol) tB, each step for 4 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 28 hours total)
    3.2  Bleaching and delipidation: Incubate sample in fresh bleaching solution B (a mixture of 30% (vol/vol) H2O2 and 100% tB at a 4:6 ratio). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours, monitor until eye pigment is fully bleached)
    3.3  Re-dehydration: Wash sample in 100% (vol/vol) tB, 3 times for 4 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)

4  **Refractive Index Matching and Clearing**
    4.1  Solvent transition: Incubate sample in a mixture of 100% tB and dichloromethane (DCM) at a 1:1 ratio. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
    4.2  Final clearing and RI matching: Transfer sample to BB-PEGASOS solution (a mixture of 40% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate and 60% (vol/vol) DCM, RI ~1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours or until fully transparent)
    4.3  Storage/Imaging medium: For long-term storage and imaging, mount the cleared eye in fresh BB-PEGASOS solution in an appropriate imaging chamber.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  **Sample Preparation and Immunolabeling**
    1.1  Permeabilization and Blocking: Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (wt/vol) donkey serum in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
    1.2  Primary Antibody Incubation: Incubation with anti-Ki67 (rabbit monoclonal, 1:500) in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 1% (wt/vol) BSA. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
    1.3  Wash: Three washes with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)
    1.4  Secondary Antibody and Dye Incubation: Incubation with donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated Phalloidin (1:200), and DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBST with 1% BSA. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
    1.5  Final Wash: Three washes with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

2  **Ce3D Clearing and Refractive Index Matching**
    2.1  Ce3D Clearing Solution Incubation: Incubation with Ce3D working solution (4% (wt/vol) N,N,N',N'-Tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine, 0.25% (wt/vol) Triton X-100, 4 M Urea in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)

    3.1  Mounting: Transfer cleared organoid to a glass-bottom dish or chamber slide filled with the final 80% Histodenz/Ce3D solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Ki67+Alexa Fluor 488, PCNA+Alexa Fluor 647, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based clearing method that is highly effective for small, dense 3D organoids (1–3 mm), preserves endogenous fluorescence and antibody epitopes well, and is compatible with multiplexed immunofluorescence. It provides excellent refractive index matching for high-resolution 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). The labeling strategy uses Ki67 (cell cycle marker) and PCNA (DNA replication marker) to distinguish proliferation states, with TO-PRO-3 as a far-red nuclear counterstain for total cell segmentation and spatial reference. This combination allows for cross-validation of drug effects on cell cycle progression vs. DNA replication activity.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  **Sample Preparation and Permeabilization**  
1.1  Wash fixed brain organoids (4% PFA, 4 ℃, overnight) with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) three times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.2  Incubate in PBST containing 20% (vol/vol) DMSO and 2.3% (wt/vol) glycine for permeabilization and quenching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3  Block with PBST containing 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum and 6% (wt/vol) BSA. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2  **Immunolabeling**  
2.1  Incubate with primary antibody cocktail: anti-Ki67 (rabbit, 1:500) and anti-PCNA (mouse, 1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.2  Wash with PBST six times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  
2.3  Incubate with secondary antibody cocktail: goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.4  Wash with PBST six times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  

3  **Nuclear Counterstaining**  
3.1  Incubate with TO-PRO-3 iodide (1:1000 in PBST) for nuclear segmentation reference. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2  Wash with PBST three times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

4  **Delipidation and Decolorization (CUBIC-L)**  
4.1  Incubate in CUBIC-L reagent 1: 25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N‑N‑diethylenetriamine, and 15 wt% Triton X-100 in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
4.2  Replace with fresh CUBIC-L reagent 1. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

5  **Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC-R+)**  
5.1  Wash with PBS three times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
5.2  Incubate in CUBIC-R+ reagent: 45 wt% sucrose, 30 wt% urea, 10 wt% 2,2′,2″‑nitrilotriethanol, and 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in distilled water (RI ≈ 1.52). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
5.3  Transfer to fresh CUBIC-R+ reagent for final equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

6  **Mounting and Imaging**  
6.1  Mount cleared organoid in CUBIC-R+ within an imaging chamber (e.g., glass-bottom dish).  
6.2  Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, Alexa Fluor 647, and TO-PRO-3.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [DAPI, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647, Ki67-Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a rapid, aqueous-based clearing method well-suited for small 3D organoids (1–3 mm). It preserves endogenous fluorescence and is compatible with immunolabeling. The protocol can be accelerated for high-throughput screening. DAPI provides total nuclear staining for cell density and volume measurement; Phalloidin outlines organoid contours and F-actin architecture; Ki67 labels proliferating cells to assess drug-induced growth arrest. Alexa Fluor conjugates ensure bright, photostable signals compatible with 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Fixation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes each)  
1.3 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Immunolabeling and Nuclear/Actin Staining  
2.1 Blocking with 5% (wt/vol) bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody anti-Ki67 (rabbit monoclonal, 1:200 in 1% BSA/PBST). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBST 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 488 goat anti-rabbit (1:500) together with Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100) and DAPI (1 µg/mL) in 1% BSA/PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

3 Tissue Clearing with CUBIC  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N,N,N',N'-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine, 15 wt% Triton X-100 in water, RI ≈ 1.45). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Wash with PBS briefly. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with CUBIC-R+ (44 wt% sucrose, 22 wt% urea, 10 wt% 2,2',2''-nitrilotriethanol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in water, RI ≈ 1.52). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
4.1 Transfer cleared organoids into CUBIC-R+ solution in an imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)  
4.2 For long-term storage, seal chamber and store at 4 ℃ protected from light.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its excellent clearing depth and high transparency in dense, fixed human skin tissue (2–3 mm thickness), strong preservation of Alexa Fluor signals through organic solvent dehydration, and compatibility with whole-mount immunolabeling. The protocol is relatively fast (days vs. weeks) and yields a high refractive index (~1.56) suitable for high-resolution light-sheet or confocal imaging of 3D nerve fibers. PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal marker) is the primary label for intraepidermal nerve fibers (IENFs); DAPI provides nuclear reference for epidermal stratification; IB4 labels endothelial cells (or a subset of sensory fibers in some species) to delineate dermal vasculature as an anatomical guide without interfering with IENF tracing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol twice, each for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours total)  
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol twice, each for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)  

2  Immunolabeling (Whole-Mount)  
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization in PBSMT (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.1% Tween-20, 5% normal donkey serum) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and biotinylated IB4 (1:200) in PBSMT for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBSMT 6 times, each for 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours total)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in PBSMT for 72 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBSMT 6 times, each for 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours total)  
2.6 Nuclear staining with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.7 Wash with PBS 3 times, each for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing  
3.1 Gradual dehydration in methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol (each step for 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours total)  
3.2 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol twice, each for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour total)  
3.4 Clearing in uDISCO solution: 42.5% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE), 42.5% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate (BB), 15% (vol/vol) diphenyl ether (DPE) for 24–48 hours until transparent. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)  

4  Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
4.1 Transfer cleared sample into fresh uDISCO solution (RI ~1.56) for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: storage until imaging)  
4.2 Mount sample in uDISCO solution in a compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its excellent transparency of dense tissues (like skin), strong fluorescence preservation of Alexa Fluor dyes, and compatibility with antibody labeling. It achieves high refractive index (RI ~1.56) for deep imaging, and its organic-solvent-based delipidation efficiently clears lipid-rich dermis while retaining epitopes for PGP9.5 (intraepidermal nerve fiber marker) and lectin (vascular network). DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial reference. The protocol is scalable for 3–4 mm skin biopsies and supports 3D co-visualization of nerves and vessels.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  **Sample Preparation and Fixation**  
1.1 Fixation in 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS, pH 7.4. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

2  **Immunolabeling**  
2.1 Permeabilization and blocking in PBST with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and biotinylated Lectin (e.g., UEA-I, 1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBST 6 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST 6 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  
2.6 Nuclear staining with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.7 Final wash with PBS 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

3  **Dehydration and Delipidation**  
3.1 Gradual dehydration in methanol/water series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol, each step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
3.2 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Delipidation in 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.4 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

4  **Refractive Index Matching and Clearing**  
4.1 Incubation in dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ~1.56) with 0.1% (wt/vol) butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) as antioxidant. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5  **Storage and Imaging**  
5.1 Store cleared sample in fresh DBE/BHT in a light-tight vial. (Temperature: RT, Time: long-term)  
5.2 Mount sample in DBE-compatible chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 647, CD31+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous-based clearing method that is highly effective for soft tissues like skin, preserves endogenous and antibody-induced fluorescence well, and achieves high transparency while maintaining tissue morphology. Its stepwise refractive index (RI) matching is gentle and compatible with subsequent 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). The labeling strategy uses PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker, Hu C/D/PGP9.5 in the marker list) for IENF identification and counting, CD31 for visualizing superficial dermal vasculature, and DAPI for nuclear reference to delineate epidermal strata and dermal papillae. This combination allows for accurate 3D quantification of IENF density per unit epidermal length/volume while correcting for tissue orientation and surface signal loss.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  **Delipidation and Decolorization (CUBIC-L)**  
1.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L reagent (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N,N,N',N'-Tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine, 15 wt% Triton X-100 in Milli-Q water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3–5 days, with gentle shaking)  
1.2 Replacement with fresh CUBIC-L reagent. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3–5 days, with gentle shaking)

2  **Wash**  
2.1 Rinse with PBS-T (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

3  **Immunolabeling**  
3.1 Blocking and permeabilization with PBS-T containing 5% normal donkey serum and 0.2% gelatin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and rat anti-CD31 (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  
3.3 Wash with PBS-T six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with gentle shaking)  
3.5 Wash with PBS-T six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  
3.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.7 Wash with PBS three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

4  **Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC-R+)**  
4.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide in Milli-Q water, RI ≈ 1.49) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% CUBIC-R+. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours, until tissue is fully cleared)

5  **Mounting and Imaging**  
5.1 Transfer cleared tissue to an imaging chamber filled with fresh CUBIC-R+. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)  
5.2 Secure tissue with a low-melting-point agarose holder (if needed for light-sheet microscopy). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Proceed to 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy) using appropriate filter sets for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, and Alexa Fluor 647.

我在进行人皮肤活检 IENF 诊断实验时发现，表皮内神经纤维信号很弱，且皮肤基底层黑色素残留造成明显光吸收、遮光和背景干扰，影响 IENF 的识别和计数。此前使用标准 CUBIC protocol，CUBIC-L 24 小时、CUBIC-RA 24 小时。请根据上述科学目标，在不引入给定标记物列表之外靶点或表外荧光团的前提下，重新选择或调整荧光/标记策略与组织透明方法。修正版应适合皮肤活检样本的表皮屏障处理、黑色素背景降低、表皮内神经纤维检测、血管网络辅助标记、低形变和三维计数分析。

请仅输出修正后的 protocol，第 1 行写明应保留或更换的荧光/标记策略和组织透明方法，随后仅列出透明处理、RI 匹配和保存/成像前处理步骤的关键试剂、条件和时间。

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 488, Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO provides rapid, high-efficiency clearing with minimal tissue deformation and excellent preservation of endogenous and labeled fluorescence, crucial for delicate intraepidermal nerve fibers (IENFs). It effectively removes lipids and melanin, reducing background absorption and autofluorescence. The chosen labeling strategy directly targets the scientific goals: PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker in the Marker list) for IENFs, Lectin (from the Dye list, targeting glycans on endothelial cells) for superficial dermal vasculature, and Hoechst for nuclear counterstain and spatial reference. Alexa Fluor dyes offer bright, photostable signals compatible with uDISCO's solvent-based environment.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Sample Preparation and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% tert-butanol (vol/vol in H2O) gradient, 1 hour per step.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours)
1.2 Incubation with 100% Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2  Immunostaining and Counterstaining
2.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% donkey serum, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail (mouse anti-PGP9.5 [Marker], 1:500; biotinylated Lectin [Dye], 1:200 in blocking solution).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.3 Washing with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST), 1 hour per wash, 3 washes total.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail (donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647, 1:500; Streptavidin Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500 in blocking solution).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Washing with PBST, 1 hour per wash, 3 washes total.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.6 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
2.7 Washing with PBS, 15 minutes per wash, 2 washes total.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3  Dehydration and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%, 100% tetrahydrofuran (THF, vol/vol in H2O) gradient, 1 hour per step.(Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours)
3.2 Incubation with 100% THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
4  Refractive Index Matching and Storage
4.1 Incubation with Dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
4.2 Storage in fresh DBE for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)

**Justification:** Ce3D is specifically optimized for *C. elegans* whole‑mount clearing, preserving endogenous fluorescence (EGFP/mCherry) exceptionally well while providing rapid and uniform clearing of the adult cuticle and internal tissues. This method is ideal for the 1‑mm adult worm to reveal 3D neuropil architecture without additional antibody labeling.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Sample Preparation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Wash fixed adult worms in 1× PBS + 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 (PBST) three times, 10 min each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes total)  
1.2 Incubate in Ce3D Permeabilization Solution (4% (wt/vol) SDS, 200 mM boric acid, pH 8.5) with gentle shaking.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4 hours)  

2  Clearing and Refractive‑Index Matching  
2.1 Rinse samples twice with 1× PBS + 0.1% Triton X‑100 to remove SDS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes total)  
2.2 Incubate in Ce3D Clearing Solution (40% (wt/vol) N‑methylacetamide, 0.6% (wt/vol) Histodenz in 1× PBS) with gentle shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Transfer to Ce3D Imaging Solution (60% (wt/vol) N‑methylacetamide, 0.6% (wt/vol) Histodenz in 1× PBS) for final refractive‑index matching (RI ≈ 1.46).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3  Mounting and Imaging  
3.1 Place cleared worm in a glass‑bottom dish or capillary filled with Ce3D Imaging Solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate)  
3.2 For long‑term storage, seal sample and store at 4 ℃ in the dark.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 1 month)

1.3 样本在 PBS 中洗涤 3 次，每次 15 分钟，以去除未结合的 DAPI。(Temperature: RT, Time: 45 minutes total)

2 脱水与透明化处理
2.1 样本在 20% (wt/vol) 果糖水溶液中孵育。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 样本在 40% (wt/vol) 果糖水溶液中孵育。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (endogenous), mCherry/RFP (endogenous), DAPI]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is specifically optimized for *C. elegans* and other small invertebrates, providing excellent clearing of the cuticle while preserving endogenous fluorescence (EGFP/mCherry) and tissue morphology. It is a simple, aqueous-based method that avoids harsh organic solvents, which is critical for maintaining the integrity of delicate neuronal structures and fluorescent proteins. The addition of DAPI provides a nuclear counterstain for spatial reference of neuronal cell bodies relative to the nerve ring and ventral nerve cord.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Sample Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed *C. elegans* adults (4% PFA) three times in 1x PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes per wash)
1.2 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in PBST for permeabilization.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

2 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D clearing solution (40% (vol/vol) N-methylacetamide, 30% (vol/vol) Histodenz, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in 0.02 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48-72 hours)

3 Nuclear Staining (Optional Auxiliary Channel)
3.1 Wash cleared sample twice in Ce3D solution diluted 1:1 with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)
3.2 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in diluted Ce3D/PBST solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
3.3 Wash sample twice in pure Ce3D clearing solution to remove excess dye.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

4 Mounting and Storage for Imaging
4.1 Transfer sample to fresh Ce3D clearing solution in an imaging chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: >1 hour for equilibration)
4.2 Seal chamber and store sample protected from light at 4 ℃ until imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), mCherry (内源), DAPI]  
**Justification:** Ce3D (Ce3D: A rapid and robust clearing method for C. elegans) is specifically developed for intact, fixed C. elegans. It is an aqueous-based method that preserves endogenous fluorescence of GFP and mCherry/RFP exceptionally well, causes minimal sample deformation, and achieves refractive index (RI) matching rapidly (within hours). It is ideal for the small size (~1 mm) and delicate neural structures (nerve ring) of C. elegans, enabling high-resolution 3D imaging of dual-color endogenous signals without the need for additional immunolabeling.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Sample Preparation and Staining
1.1 Wash fixed C. elegans samples three times in 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (PBST) for 10 minutes each.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes total)
1.2 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBST for nuclear counterstaining.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
1.3 Wash samples three times in PBST for 10 minutes each to remove excess DAPI.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes total)

2  Dehydration and Clearing
2.1 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) N-Methylacetamide (NMA) in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 40% (wt/vol) NMA in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 60% (wt/vol) NMA in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488/647, HuC/D (primary) + Alexa Fluor 568 (secondary), DAPI]  
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is an aqueous, simple, and rapid clearing method that preserves fluorescence of protein-based labels (e.g., Alexa Fluor dyes) and small-molecule dyes (e.g., Phalloidin) exceptionally well. It is ideal for small, delicate samples like 5 dpf zebrafish larvae, as it avoids harsh organic solvents and detergents that could damage F-actin structures. The refractive index (RI ~1.52) achieved with SeeDB2S is suitable for high-resolution confocal or light-sheet imaging of the entire larva. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereociliary bundles, while the pan-neuronal marker HuC/D robustly labels hair cells and neurons in the lateral line neuromasts, allowing for cell identification and counting. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  **Sample Preparation and Permeabilization**
    1.1 Wash fixed 5 dpf zebrafish larvae 3x with PBS + 0.1% Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min each)
    1.2 Permeabilize with 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2  **Immunostaining and F-actin Labeling**
    2.1 Block with 5% normal goat serum in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
    2.2 Incubate with primary antibody (mouse anti-HuC/D, 1:100) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
    2.3 Wash 5x with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
    2.4 Incubate with secondary antibody (goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 568, 1:500) and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488/647 (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
    2.5 Wash 5x with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
    2.6 Incubate with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min)
    2.7 Wash 3x with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min each)

3  **SeeDB2 Optical Clearing**
    3.1 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) fructose in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
    3.2 Incubation with 40% (wt/vol) fructose in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
    3.3 Incubation with 60% (wt/vol) fructose in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
    3.4 Incubation with 80% (wt/vol) fructose in dH2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
    3.5 Incubation with SeeDB2S solution (137.5 g fructose + 0.5 mL α-thioglycerol per 100 mL dH2O, RI ~1.52). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12-24 hours)

4  **Refractive Index Matching and Mounting**
    4.1 Transfer sample to a fresh dish containing SeeDB2S solution for imaging.
    4.2 Mount the larva in SeeDB2S within an imaging chamber (e.g., glass-bottom dish) using a spacer to prevent compression.

**Chosen Method:** SeeDB2
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647, Myosin VIIa-Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]
**Justification:** SeeDB2 is an aqueous, simple, and rapid clearing method that is highly compatible with fluorescent proteins and small molecule dyes like Phalloidin. It does not require organic solvents or harsh delipidation, which is crucial for preserving the delicate F-actin structures (stereocilia bundles) in hair cells. The protocol is gentle and maintains good fluorescence, making it ideal for the small, fixed 5 dpf zebrafish larvae (~4 mm). Phalloidin directly labels F-actin for the stereocilia bundle. An antibody against Myosin VIIa, a well-established hair cell identity marker in zebrafish, is used to confirm hair cell location and count. DAPI labels nuclei for overall orientation.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Immunostaining and F-actin Labeling (Post-Fixation)
1.1 Permeabilization and Blocking: Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.2 Primary Antibody Incubation: Incubation with rabbit anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody (1:200 dilution) in blocking solution (0.1% Triton X-100, 1% normal goat serum in PBS).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.3 Wash: Wash with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (PBT) 5 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)
1.4 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Incubation: Incubation with goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500 dilution) and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100 dilution) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.5 Wash: Wash with PBT 5 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)
1.6 Nuclear Stain: Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
1.7 Final Wash: Wash with PBS 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes per wash)

2  SeeDB2 Optical Clearing
2.1 Dehydration: Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) fructose in 0.5% α-thioglycerol aqueous solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.2 Incubation with 40% (wt/vol) fructose in 0.5% α-thioglycerol aqueous solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.3 Incubation with 60% (wt/vol) fructose in 0.5% α-thioglycerol aqueous solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.4 Incubation with 80% (wt/vol) fructose in 0.5% α-thioglycerol aqueous solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.5 RI Matching and Clearing: Incubation with SeeDB2S solution (137.5% (wt/vol) fructose, 0.5% α-thioglycerol in water, RI ~1.52).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12-24 hours)

3  Mounting for Imaging
3.1 Mounting: Transfer sample into a glass-bottom dish filled with fresh SeeDB2S solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)
3.2 Sealing: Seal the dish with a coverslip and parafilm or VALAP to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, anti-acetylated Tubulin-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing capability and strong preservation of endogenous fluorescence (e.g., GFP/YFP) and antibody/Phalloidin signals in small, delicate samples like zebrafish larvae. It achieves high transparency and a high refractive index (RI ~1.56), ideal for high-resolution 3D imaging of deep structures. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in hair cell stereociliary bundles. Anti-acetylated Tubulin is a well-established marker for neuronal axons, perfectly suited to visualize the lateral line nerve fibers and their innervation patterns. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for cellular orientation.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2  Immunostaining and F-actin Labeling
2.1 Rehydration through a graded methanol series: 80%, 50%, 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, 3 times)
2.3 Blocking and permeabilization with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 and 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.4 Incubation with primary antibody (mouse anti-acetylated Tubulin, 1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, 4 times)
2.6 Incubation with secondary antibody (goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647, 1:500) and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.7 Wash with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, 4 times)
2.8 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.9 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes, 3 times)

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing
3.1 Dehydration through a graded methanol series: 30%, 50%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, twice)
3.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Diphenyl ether (DPE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, until sample is fully cleared)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Mounting
4.1 Mount the cleared sample in fresh 100% (vol/vol) Diphenyl ether (DPE, RI ~1.56) in a suitable imaging chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: stable for imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** ScaleS (modified protocol with gradient dehydration and RI matching)
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, HuC/D-Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI] # Phalloidin for F-actin, HuC/D as a pan-neuronal marker to help identify neuromast context, DAPI for nuclei.
**Justification:** The original problem was tissue swelling and fluorescence loss with a rapid ScaleS0-to-S4 transition. ScaleS is still an excellent choice for small, delicate zebrafish larvae as it is a gentle, aqueous-based method. The key is to introduce a gradual dehydration series (methanol gradient) before ScaleS0 to minimize osmotic shock and tissue swelling. This revised protocol preserves the fluorescence of Alexa Fluor-conjugated probes (Phalloidin, antibody) and endogenous GFP/YFP from transgenic lines. It provides excellent clearing for 3D imaging of structures as fine as stereocilia bundles while maintaining tissue morphology.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Post-fixation Wash and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed 5 dpf larvae in 1x PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 15 minutes, 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 45 minutes total)
1.2 Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2  Immunostaining and Phalloidin Labeling
2.1 Blocking in 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) in PBST for 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody (mouse anti-HuC/D, 1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.3 Wash in PBST for 15 minutes, 4 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647, 1:500) and Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Wash in PBST for 15 minutes, 4 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.6 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS for 30 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
2.7 Final wash in PBS for 15 minutes, 2 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

3  Gradient Dehydration (to prevent swelling)
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes, 2 times)

4  ScaleS-based Optical Clearing
4.1 Incubation with ScaleS0 solution [4M urea, 10% (wt/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100]. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
4.2 Incubation with ScaleS4 solution [4M urea, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100]. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)

5  Refractive Index Matching and Mounting for Imaging
5.1 Transfer sample to ScaleView-A2 (Olympus) or 80% (vol/vol) ScaleS4 / 20% (vol/vol) glycerol for RI matching (RI ~1.38-1.40). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.2 Mount the cleared larva in the chosen mounting medium in a glass-bottom dish or chamber for confocal/light-sheet microscopy.

3.1 Incubate samples in 50% (vol/vol) ClearSee / 50% (vol/vol) 2,2'-Thiodiethanol (TDE) solution without shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
3.2 Incubate samples in 97% (vol/vol) TDE in water (refractive index ~1.52) without shaking for final RI matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
3.3 Mount sample in 97% TDE in a suitable imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional ability to preserve tissue morphology and fluorescence in large, dense tissues like skeletal muscle. It achieves high transparency and minimal shrinkage through a graded dehydration and delipidation process, followed by refractive index matching with dibenzyl ether (DBE). This is critical for maintaining the integrity of the neuromuscular junction (NMJ) structure and preventing signal loss. The labeling strategy directly targets the scientific goals: alpha-bungarotoxin (conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647) specifically labels postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) for NMJ localization and morphology analysis. Phalloidin (conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488) labels F-actin, outlining muscle fibers to provide spatial context and assess fiber morphology. DAPI stains nuclei, aiding in tissue orientation.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS for 1 hour. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol for 1 hour. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) for refractive index matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

3  Labeling (Performed after Step 1.4, before Step 1.5)
3.1 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum in PBST for 6 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
3.3 Incubation with alpha-bungarotoxin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:200 dilution in blocking solution) for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
3.4 Incubation with Phalloidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200 dilution in PBST) and DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBST) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
3.5 Wash with PBST, three times for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)
3.6 Resume dehydration starting at Step 1.1.

**Justification:** CUBIC is an aqueous, hydrophilic clearing method that is highly effective for soft tissues like skeletal muscle. The protocol is scalable and well-suited for the provided tissue dimensions (8x5x3 mm). The chosen labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goals: alpha-bungarotoxin (AChR ligand) for the postsynaptic receptor clusters, beta-III tubulin (TUJ1) antibody for the motor nerve terminals and axons, and DAPI for nuclei to provide spatial context.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed tissue in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours, changing solution every 2 hours.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.2 Incubation in PBST with 20% (vol/vol) DMSO and 2.3% (wt/vol) glycine for 24 hours to quench autofluorescence and enhance permeability.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Wash tissue in PBST for 12 hours, changing solution every 4 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2  Immunostaining and AChR Labeling
2.1 Blocking in PBST containing 6% (vol/vol) normal goat serum and 10% (vol/vol) DMSO for 48 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Primary antibody incubation: Incubate in blocking solution containing rabbit anti-beta-III Tubulin (TUJ1) antibody (1:500 dilution) for 7 days.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.3 Wash in PBST for 24 hours, changing solution 4-6 times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Secondary antibody incubation: Incubate in blocking solution containing goat anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500 dilution) for 7 days.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.5 Wash in PBST for 24 hours, changing solution 4-6 times.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.6 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (1:500 dilution in PBST) for 48 hours to label AChRs.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.7 Incubation with DAPI (1:1000 dilution in PBST) for 24 hours to label nuclei.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.8 Final wash in PBST for 12 hours, changing solution 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3  Tissue Clearing (CUBIC Reagent-1)
3.1 Incubation in 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R1 (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% Quadrol, 15 wt% Triton X-100 in dH2O) in PBST for 24 hours.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
3.2 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R1 for 7-14 days until tissue is transparent, replacing solution every 3-4 days.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7-14 days)

4  Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC Reagent-2)
4.1 Wash tissue in PBS for 12 hours to remove residual CUBIC-R1.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
4.2 Incubation in 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R2 (50 wt% sucrose, 25 wt% urea, 10 wt% 2,2',2''-nitrilotriethanol, 0.1% v/v Triton X-100 in dH2O) in PBS for 24 hours.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.3 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R2 (RI ~1.48) for 3-7 days until fully cleared and RI-matched for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3-7 days)

5  Mounting and Imaging
5.1 Mount the cleared tissue in a chamber filled with fresh 100% CUBIC-R2.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)
5.2 Proceed with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D imaging.
