**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [alpha-bungarotoxin, beta-III Tubulin (TUJ1), DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional tissue shrinkage inhibition (critical for preserving NMJ architecture in muscle), high transparency, and strong compatibility with lipophilic dyes and antibody labeling. It preserves fluorescence well and is suitable for whole-mount tissues of this size. Alpha-bungarotoxin directly labels AChRs. Beta-III Tubulin (TUJ1) antibody labels the motor neuron axons and terminals. DAPI labels nuclei for spatial reference. This combination allows simultaneous visualization of postsynaptic AChR clusters, presynaptic nerve terminals, and overall tissue architecture with minimal distortion.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Labeling
1.1 Wash fixed gastrocnemius muscle sample in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)
1.2 Permeabilization and blocking with incubation in PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Primary antibody incubation with mouse anti-beta-III Tubulin (TUJ1) diluted 1:500 in PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 1% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.4 Wash sample in PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)
1.5 Secondary antibody and alpha-bungarotoxin co-incubation with goat anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (1:200) in PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 1% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
1.6 Wash sample in PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 3 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)
1.7 Nuclear staining with incubation in PBS containing 1 µg/mL DAPI.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
1.8 Final wash in PBS, 2 times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Dehydration in a graded methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in H2O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each step)
2.2 Delipidation with incubation in fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: Overnight)
2.3 Delipidation with incubation in fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: Overnight)

3  uDISCO Clearing
3.1 Incubation in a 1:2 mixture of Tetrahydrofuran (THF) to methanol (vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.2 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.3 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) Tetrahydrofuran (THF).(Temperature: RT, Time: Overnight)
3.4 Incubation in a 4:1 mixture of Benzyl Ether (DBE) to Tetrahydrofuran (THF) (vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.5 Final clearing and RI matching with incubation in 100% (vol/vol) Benzyl Ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional ability to render large, dense, and complex tissues like the whole mouse stomach transparent while strongly preserving endogenous fluorescence and the signal from antibody labeling. The labeling strategy uses PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) to visualize all nerve fibers, combined with Lectin to outline tissue architecture (e.g., mucosal glands, muscle layers), and Hoechst for nuclear counterstaining. This combination allows for the comprehensive 3D mapping and comparative analysis of neural density, fiber trajectory, branching complexity, and spatial localization within different gastric regions and layers.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed stomach sample in 1x PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-Tx) on a shaker. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution: 1x PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 20% (vol/vol) Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO). (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

2  Immunofluorescence and Counterstaining
2.1 Blocking by incubation in blocking solution: 1x PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 6% (wt/vol) Donkey Serum. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Primary antibody incubation: Incubation in blocking solution containing rabbit anti-PGP9.5 primary antibody (1:500) and Biotinylated Lectin (e.g., UEA-I or WGA, 10 µg/mL). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.3 Wash in 1x PBS-Tx on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with solution changed every 8 hours)
2.4 Secondary antibody and streptavidin incubation: Incubation in blocking solution containing Donkey anti-Rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), Streptavidin conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), and Hoechst 33342 (5 µg/mL). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.5 Wash in 1x PBS-Tx on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with solution changed every 8 hours)

3  Dehydration and Delipidation
3.1 Gradual dehydration in an ascending series of tert-Butanol (tB) in 1x PBS: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% (vol/vol) tB. Incubate at each step on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per step)
3.2 Final dehydration in 100% (vol/vol) anhydrous tB. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
3.3 Delipidation and initial clearing by incubation in Dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

The labeling strategy uses PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal marker, Hu C/D) to outline the entire neural network, TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) to label sympathetic/adrenergic fibers, and Phalloidin (F-actin) to delineate muscle layers as an anatomical reference. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain. This combination allows comprehensive mapping of nerve fiber entry, branching, terminal coverage, and regional/laminal density comparisons.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)  

2  Delipidation and Bleaching (Optional)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Wash with 100% (vol/vol) methanol, 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

3  Rehydration and Blocking  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBS-T), 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
3.6 Incubation with blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 6% normal donkey serum, 10 mg/ml heparin). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

4  Immunostaining and Counterstaining  
4.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and mouse anti-TH (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
4.2 Wash with PBS-T, 6 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  
4.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), plus Alexa Fluor 555-conjugated Phalloidin (1:200) and DAPI (5 µg/ml) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
4.4 Wash with PBS-T, 6 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

5  Dehydration for Clearing  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated three times)  

6  uDISCO Clearing and RI Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, until tissue is transparent)  

7  Storage and Imaging  
7.1 Store cleared stomach in fresh 100% DBE in a light-tight container at 4 ℃ until imaging.  
7.2 For imaging, mount sample in DBE within an appropriate imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 647, Phalloidin-Alexa Fluor 488]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing depth and high transparency in large, dense organs like the stomach, its strong compatibility with lipophilic dyes and antibody labeling, and its excellent preservation of endogenous and conjugated fluorophores (e.g., Alexa Fluor series). The method provides a stable, durable refractive index-matched state ideal for high-resolution 3D imaging (e.g., light-sheet microscopy). The labeling strategy uses PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker, Hu C/D/PGP9.5 in the provided list) to comprehensively label all nerve fibers and terminals, combined with Phalloidin to specifically label F-actin, providing a clear structural reference for the circular and longitudinal muscle layers. This combination directly addresses the core goal of mapping the 3D spatial relationship between vagal nerve endings and the gastric muscular architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM, Sigma 270997) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2  Immunostaining and Phalloidin Labeling
2.1 Rehydration through a graded methanol series: 80%, 50%, 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated three times)
2.3 Blocking and permeabilization in PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, and 3% (wt/vol) BSA.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Primary antibody incubation with rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBS-T.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours, repeated six times)
2.6 Secondary antibody and phalloidin incubation with donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated Phalloidin (1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.7 Wash with PBS-T.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 2 hours, repeated six times)

3  Final Dehydration and Solvent Exchange
3.1 Dehydration through a graded methanol series in PBS: 30%, 50%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated once)

4  Clearing and Refractive Index Matching
4.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, or until fully transparent)
4.4 Storage and imaging in fresh 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl Ether (DBE, RI ~1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)

The chosen markers target pan-neuronal (PGP9.5) and adrenergic/sympathetic (TH) components, providing a dual-channel view of the neural network. DAPI stains nuclei for anatomical context. Alexa Fluor dyes are bright, photostable, and compatible with iDISCO+ clearing and common imaging setups.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2  Bleaching (Optional, for strong autofluorescence reduction)
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12-24 hours)

3  Rehydration and Blocking
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)
3.5 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBTx).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 3 times)
3.6 Incubation with blocking solution: PBTx containing 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, then Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12-24 hours)

4  Primary Antibody Staining
4.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in blocking solution (e.g., Rabbit anti-PGP9.5 1:500, Mouse anti-TH 1:500).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48-72 hours with gentle agitation)

5  Washing
5.1 Wash with PBTx.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeat 8 times over 24 hours)

6  Secondary Antibody and Nuclear Staining
6.1 Incubation with secondary antibody and nuclear stain cocktail in blocking solution (e.g., Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 1:500, Donkey anti-Mouse Alexa Fluor 488 1:500, DAPI 1:1000).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48-72 hours with gentle agitation)

7  Post-Staining Washing
7.1 Wash with PBTx.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeat 8 times over 24 hours)

8  Final Dehydration
8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)
8.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)
8.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)
8.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 20 minutes)
8.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat twice)

9  Delipidation and Clearing
9.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
9.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeat once)

10 Refractive Index Matching
10.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, repeat until tissue is fully cleared and sink)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [EGFP (内源), tdTomato (内源), MAP2+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency and strong tissue shrinkage (up to ~65% volume reduction), which is advantageous for imaging large samples like whole mouse brains with high resolution. It preserves endogenous fluorescence (EGFP, tdTomato) very well and is compatible with immunolabeling for fine structures. The protocol is relatively fast (days vs. weeks) and uses common organic solvents. Adding an antibody against MAP2 (a dendritic marker) with a far-red fluorophore (Alexa Fluor 647) allows simultaneous visualization of long-range axonal projections (via endogenous signals) and local dendritic architecture in target regions, meeting the dual requirement of tracing and structural analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  **Dehydration and Delipidation**
    1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
    1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
    1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
    1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)
    1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
    1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2  **Refractive Index Matching and Clearing**
    2.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) containing 0.4% (vol/vol) Quadrol (N,N,N',N'-Tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24-48 hours, until transparent)

3  **Immunolabeling (Optional, for MAP2)**
    *Note: Immunolabeling is performed after Step 1.4 (100% methanol) and before Step 1.5 (DCM). The sample is rehydrated for labeling.*
    3.1 Rehydration through a descending methanol series: 80%, 50%, 30% methanol in PBS, each step.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
    3.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBS-T).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 3 times)
    3.3 Blocking and permeabilization in PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 10% normal donkey serum, and 0.1% sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
    3.4 Incubation with primary antibody (Chicken anti-MAP2, 1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72-96 hours with gentle shaking)
    3.5 Wash with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat 6 times over 24 hours)
    3.6 Incubation with secondary antibody (Donkey anti-Chicken Alexa Fluor 647, 1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72-96 hours with gentle shaking)
    3.7 Wash with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat 6 times over 24 hours)
    3.8 Dehydration through an ascending methanol series: 30%, 50%, 80%, 100% methanol in PBS, each step.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
    3.9 Proceed to Step 1.5 (66% DCM in methanol).

4  **Storage and Imaging**
    4.1 Store cleared brain in fresh DBE/Quadrol solution in a light-tight container.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinitely)
    4.2 For imaging, mount the sample in the same DBE/Quadrol solution within an appropriate imaging chamber.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 脱水与淬灭
1.1 梯度脱水：依次在 30%、50%、70%、80%、96%、100% (vol/vol) 叔丁醇水溶液中孵育，每步 1 小时。(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hours)

2.2 封闭：在含 10% (vol/vol) 正常驴血清和 0.2% Triton X-100 的 PBST 中孵育。(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
2.3 一抗孵育：在含 1:500 兔抗 MAP2 抗体和 0.2% Triton X-100 的 PBST 中孵育。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.4 洗涤：在 PBST 中洗涤，每天更换 3 次溶液。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 days)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos (primary antibody) + Alexa Fluor 647, NeuN (primary antibody) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency for large, dense tissues (whole mouse brain and tongue) while strongly preserving endogenous and antibody-conjugated fluorescence over long periods—critical for capturing activity-dependent c-Fos signal across multiple brain regions. Its organic-solvent-based delipidation and RI matching with DBE provide rapid, deep clearing and high refractive index (RI ~1.56), enabling high-resolution light-sheet imaging of whole organs with preserved 3D spatial relationships between the tongue and brain. DAPI provides nuclear reference for registration, while NeuN labels mature neurons to contextualize c-Fos+ activated cells.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  Dehydration and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)  
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2  Immunostaining (performed after rehydration)  
2.1 Rehydration through graded methanol series: 80%, 50%, 30% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 3 times)  
2.3 Blocking with PBST containing 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.1% sodium azide (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-c-Fos (1:500) + mouse anti-NeuN (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.5 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat 4 times)  
2.6 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) + donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.7 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeat 4 times)  
2.8 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.9 Wash with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat twice)  

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing  
3.1 Dehydration through graded methanol series: 30%, 50%, 80%, 100% methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)  
3.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

4  Refractive Index Matching  
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, repeat once until tissue is fully transparent)  

5  Storage and Imaging  
5.1 Store cleared samples in fresh DBE in light-tight vials at 4 ℃ until imaging.  
5.2 Mount sample in DBE-compatible chamber for light-sheet microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [c-Fos (primary) + Alexa Fluor 488, Npas4 (primary) + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected for its proven effectiveness in clearing whole adult mouse brains and other large, dense organs (like tongue), enabling deep antibody penetration and high-resolution 3D imaging. The methanol-based dehydration and delipidation steps are robust for removing lipids from both neural and muscular/connective tissues. Crucially, iDISCO+ includes a permeabilization/antigen-retrieval step (using methanol and H2O2) and a long antibody incubation in a permeable, detergent-based solution, which directly addresses the original protocol's weaknesses of poor permeabilization, weak signal, and incomplete clearing. The chosen labeling strategy uses two different Alexa Fluor conjugates to distinguish the two immediate early gene (IEG) products (c-Fos and Npas4) in key brain regions (MTN, LC, PVT, NAcSh) and tongue neuromuscular junctions. Lectin (IB4) labels vasculature/endothelium, providing anatomical context. DAPI stains nuclei. All fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488, 555, 647) are compatible with iDISCO+'s solvent-based clearing and exhibit good photostability.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration & Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.7 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% H2O2 in methanol (1 volume 30% H2O2 to 5 volumes MeOH). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)

2  Delipidation & Solvent Transition
2.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
2.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

3  Rehydration & Blocking
3.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Incubation with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBTx). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.7 Incubation with PBTx containing 10% (vol/vol) DMSO and 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) for blocking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

4  Primary Antibody Staining
4.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail in PBTx containing 10% DMSO, 3% NDS, and 0.02% sodium azide. Cocktail: rabbit anti-c-Fos (1:500), goat anti-Npas4 (1:300), IB4-Alexa Fluor 555 (1:200). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)

5  Washing

5.2 Wash with PBTx containing 10% DMSO. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.3 Wash with PBTx containing 10% DMSO. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.4 Wash with PBTx containing 10% DMSO. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
5.5 Wash with PBTx containing 10% DMSO. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

6  Secondary Antibody & Nuclear Staining
6.1 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail in PBTx containing 10% DMSO, 3% NDS. Cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle shaking)
6.2 Wash with PBTx containing 10% DMSO. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 5 times)
6.3 Wash with PBTx. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 3 times)
6.4 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBTx. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

7  Final Dehydration & Clearing
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled H2O. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 2 times)
7.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
7.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeat 2 times)
7.8 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours for refractive index matching and storage until imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [DiI, DiD, DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing depth and tissue shrinkage minimization, which is critical for preserving the long-range 3D spatial relationships between the spinal cord, thalamus, and somatosensory cortex. It offers high transparency and refractive index matching suitable for high-resolution light-sheet microscopy. The method is compatible with lipophilic dyes like DiI and DiD, which are ideal for long-term, stable labeling of neuronal tracts. DAPI is included as a nuclear counterstain to facilitate precise anatomical registration of thalamic nuclei and cortical layers, without interfering with the primary tract-tracing signals.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Labeling
1.1 Post-fixation and washing of dissected spinal cord, thalamus, and somatosensory cortex in 4% PFA (vol/vol in PBS) for 24 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Rinse tissue three times with 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4) for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.3 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
1.4 Rinse tissue three times with PBS to remove excess DAPI. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.5 Preparation of DiI and DiD crystals. Focal application of DiI crystals to the dorsal root entry zone of one spinal segment and DiD crystals to an adjacent or functionally distinct entry zone to label separate ascending pathways. (Temperature: RT, Time: Application step)
1.6 Incubation in PBS in the dark to allow dye diffusion along axons. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 4-6 weeks)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Gradual dehydration in a series of tert-butanol (tB) solutions: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, and 100% (vol/vol in H2O). Incubate in each solution for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 84 hours total)
2.2 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 3 hours to remove remaining lipids and water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

3  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation in pure dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG) for refractive index matching and final clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, or until tissue is fully transparent)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 647, CGRP+Alexa Fluor 488, IB4+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it is highly effective for lipid-rich tissues (e.g., white adipose tissue) by combining strong delipidation with excellent fluorescence preservation and high transparency. Its organic‑solvent‑based approach efficiently removes lipids while maintaining the integrity of fluorescent protein signals and antibody conjugates over cm‑scale samples. The chosen labeling strategy uses PGP9.5 (pan‑neuronal marker) to visualize the entire nerve network, CGRP (calcitonin gene‑related peptide, a marker for sensory fibers) to specifically identify sensory fibers, IB4 (lectin) to label vascular endothelium for spatial reference, and DAPI for nuclear counterstain. This combination allows direct comparison of sensory fiber distribution against the total nerve network, addressing the scientific goal of quantifying spatial占比 and distribution patterns.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Immunostaining (Post‑fixation)
1.1 Permeabilization and blocking: Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Primary antibody incubation: Incubation with rabbit anti‑PGP9.5 (1:500) and rabbit anti‑CGRP (1:300) in PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 and 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.3 Wash: Three washes with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.4 Secondary antibody and lectin incubation: Incubation with donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), and IB4‑Alexa Fluor 555 (10 µg/mL) in PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100 and 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.5 Wash: Three washes with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.6 Nuclear staining: Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
1.7 Final wash: Two washes with PBS, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Gradient dehydration: Sequential incubation in 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, and 100% (vol/vol) tert‑butanol (t‑BuOH) in water, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 14 hours)
2.2 Delipidation and dehydration: Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.3 Final dehydration: Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) t‑BuOH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

3  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution: Immersion in dibenzyl ether (DBE) containing 0.4% (wt/vol) 2,2′‑thiodiethanol (TDE) as an antioxidant. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24‑48 hours, until tissue is transparent)

4  Storage and Imaging
4.1 Storage: Store cleared tissue in fresh uDISCO clearing solution (DBE + 0.4% TDE) in a light‑tight container. (Temperature: RT, for up to several months)
4.2 Mounting for imaging: Mount tissue in a custom‑made or commercial imaging chamber filled with uDISCO clearing solution. Seal chamber to prevent evaporation.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP (primary) + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 (primary) + Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4) + Alexa Fluor 555, Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing depth and tissue shrinkage minimization, which is crucial for preserving the 3D architecture of a relatively large (1 cm³) fixed adipose tissue block. It provides high transparency and refractive index matching suitable for high-resolution light-sheet microscopy. The chosen labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goal: PGP9.5 is a pan-neuronal marker to label the entire nerve network, while CGRP specifically labels the sensory nerve fibers. IB4 (lectin) is included as an optional vascular/structural reference channel. Hoechst provides nuclear counterstain for spatial orientation.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Permeabilization
1.1 Wash fixed tissue in PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
1.2 Incubation with permeabilization solution (PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 20% (vol/vol) DMSO) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

2  Immunostaining
2.1 Blocking with blocking solution (PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-CGRP (1:500), chicken anti-PGP9.5 (1:500), and IB4-Alexa Fluor 555 (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 5% DMSO, 3% donkey serum) for 7 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.3 Wash in PBS-T with gentle shaking, refreshing wash buffer every 12 hours for a total of 3 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-chicken Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer for 7 days. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.5 Wash in PBS-T with gentle shaking, refreshing wash buffer every 12 hours for a total of 3 days. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 days)
2.6 Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (1:1000) in PBS for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

3  Dehydration and Delipidation
3.1 Gradual dehydration in tert-butanol (tB) series: 30% (vol/vol), 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, and 100% tB in H2O, 12 hours per step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 84 hours total)
3.2 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) for 3 hours to remove remaining lipids and water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
4.1 Incubation in dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) for refractive index matching and final clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, or until tissue is fully transparent)

5  Mounting and Imaging
5.1 Mount cleared tissue sample in a custom imaging chamber filled with fresh DBE. (Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)
5.2 Proceed with light-sheet or confocal microscopy for 3D imaging.

2  Dehydration
2.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
2.5 Repeat incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 min)

5  Storage and Imaging
5.1 Store cleared tissue in fresh DBE in a light‑tight container at 4 ℃ until imaging.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 647, CGRP+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it is highly effective for clearing large, lipid-rich tissues like subcutaneous white adipose tissue (scWAT). It achieves rapid and deep delipidation and dehydration, which is critical for the opaque, high-fat sample described. The method preserves fluorescence well and provides excellent refractive index (RI) matching for deep 3D imaging. The chosen labeling strategy uses PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) and CGRP (a marker for specific sensory nerve fibers) with bright, photostable Alexa Fluor dyes, enabling simultaneous dual-channel detection of the target neural networks. DAPI is included for nuclear counterstaining to delineate tissue architecture (e.g., fat lobules).

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Immunostaining (Post-Fixation)
1.1 Wash fixed tissue block 3 times with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)
1.2 Block and permeabilize in PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500) and goat anti-CGRP (1:300) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking)
1.4 Wash tissue block 6 times with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle shaking, protected from light)
1.6 Wash tissue block 6 times with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)
1.7 Incubate with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBST for nuclear staining. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Incubation with a graded methanol series in distilled water: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol, each step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
2.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, for final delipidation and dehydration)

3  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) for RI matching and final clearing. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours or until tissue is fully transparent)

4  Storage and Imaging
4.1 Store cleared tissue in fresh DBE in a light-tight container at 4 ℃ until imaging.
4.2 For imaging, mount the cleared tissue block in a chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 647, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is chosen for its exceptional ability to clear dense, mineralized tissues like bone while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody signals over long periods, which is critical for studying intricate neural networks within the calcified matrix. It achieves high transparency and a high refractive index (RI ~1.56), ideal for light-sheet microscopy of large, opaque samples. The labeling strategy combines PGP9.5 (a pan-neuronal marker) to trace all nerve fibers, Osteocalcin to label the bone matrix for spatial context, Lectin to highlight vasculature and meningeal surfaces, and DAPI for nuclei. This multiplexing allows for the simultaneous visualization of nerves, their bony conduits, vascular relationships, and cellular architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Decalcification, Delipidation, and Dehydration
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA, pH 7.4, on a shaker.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days, with solution change every 2 days)
1.2 Incubation with 20% (wt/vol) sucrose in PBS for cryoprotection.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
1.3 Incubation with a graded methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol (vol/vol in H2O), each step on a shaker.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
1.4 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)
2  Immunostaining and Nuclear Labeling
2.1 Rehydration through a reverse graded methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol (vol/vol in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
2.2 Permeabilization and blocking with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal donkey serum, and 1% BSA.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours on a shaker)
2.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500), goat anti-Osteocalcin (1:200), and biotinylated Lectin (e.g., Griffonia Simplicifolia Lectin I, 10 µg/mL) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days on a shaker)
2.4 Washing with PBS containing 0.1% Tween-20 (PBS-T).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)
2.5 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days on a shaker)
2.6 Washing with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 6 times over 24 hours)
2.7 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.8 Washing with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)
3  Final Dehydration and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with a graded methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol (vol/vol in H2O), each step on a shaker.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
3.2 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)
3.3 Incubation with 66% Dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% Methanol (vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)
3.5 Incubation with Diethyl Ether (freshly opened).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
3.6 Incubation with uDISCO clearing solution: 85% (vol/vol) Diethyl Ether, 15% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl Ether, with 0.1% (vol/vol) antioxidant (e.g., 2,6-Di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24-48 hours, until samples are transparent)

4.1 Mounting in fresh uDISCO clearing solution for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)
4.2 Storage in sealed glass vials filled with uDISCO solution, protected from light.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Long-term)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency in dense, mineralized tissues (including bone) through a combination of dehydration, delipidation, and refractive index matching with dibenzyl ether (DBE). It preserves endogenous and antibody-induced fluorescence well, is compatible with whole-organ clearing of mouse skull and femur, and allows deep imaging of neural and vascular structures. The labeling strategy uses an anti-CGRP antibody (to specifically label sensory nerve fibers) combined with Alexa Fluor 647, while Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum lectin) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 labels vascular endothelial luminal surfaces. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for cellular reference. This combination enables simultaneous 3D mapping of nerves, vessels, bone pores, and marrow cavities.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Sample Preparation and Decalcification  
1.1 Post-fixation in 4% PFA (vol/vol in PBS) for 24 hours at 4°C. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Gentle decalcification in 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, refreshed every 2 days. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days)  
1.3 Wash in PBS with 0.1% Triton X-100 (PBST) 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

2  Immunostaining and Vascular Labeling  
2.1 Permeabilization and blocking in PBST with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody: rabbit anti-CGRP (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
2.3 Wash in PBST 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Lectin-Alexa Fluor 488 (20 µg/mL) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
2.5 Wash in PBST 6 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
2.6 Nuclear staining with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBST for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.7 Final wash in PBST 3 × 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

3  Dehydration  
3.1 Gradual dehydration in methanol/water series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol, each for 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours)  
3.2 Additional incubation in 100% methanol overnight. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

4  Delipidation and Clearing  
4.1 Incubation in 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.2 Incubation in 100% DCM for 15 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation in 100% dibenzyl ether (DBE) for refractive index matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5  Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
5.1 Transfer cleared sample to fresh DBE for storage and imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP (primary) + Alexa Fluor 647 (secondary), β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, primary) + Alexa Fluor 488 (secondary), DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS (Polyethylene glycol‑Associated Solvent System) is explicitly designed for hard, mineralized tissues. It combines strong decalcification (EDTA), delipidation (tert‑butanol), and RI matching (BB‑PEG) in a sequential manner, which is ideal for intact bone, bone marrow, and meninges. It preserves fluorescence well, allows deep antibody penetration due to its decalcifying and softening steps, and achieves high transparency (RI ~1.56) suitable for high‑resolution 3D imaging of dense bone. The chosen markers directly address the scientific goal: CGRP for sensory fibers, β‑III Tubulin (TUJ1) for pan‑neuronal labeling, and DAPI for nuclear counterstain. Alexa Fluor dyes are robust, compatible with PEGASOS, and within the allowed list.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Decalcification and Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation in 20% (wt/vol) EDTA (pH 7.4) in PBS with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days, solution changed daily)  
1.2 Wash in PBS for 2 hours, three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours total)  
1.3 Dehydration in graded tert‑butanol (t‑BuOH) series: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 100% (vol/vol in H₂O), each step with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per step)  
1.4 Final dehydration in fresh 100% tert‑butanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching (Optional, if autofluorescence is high)  
2.1 Incubation in 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in tert‑butanol with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Wash in fresh 100% tert‑butanol twice. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

3 Immunostaining (Performed in permeable state after dehydration)  
3.1 Rehydration in descending tert‑butanol series: 90%, 70%, 50%, 30% (vol/vol in PBS), each step with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)  
3.2 Wash in PBS‑T (0.2% Triton X‑100 in PBS) three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  
3.3 Blocking and permeabilization in PBS‑T containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3 M glycine. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.4 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti‑CGRP (1:500) and mouse anti‑β‑III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) in blocking solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.5 Wash in PBS‑T six times over 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total)  
3.6 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti‑mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution with gentle shaking. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)  
3.7 Wash in PBS‑T six times over 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours total)  
3.8 Optional nuclear staining: Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
3.9 Wash in PBS three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)  

4 Final Dehydration and Clearing  
4.1 Dehydration in ascending tert‑butanol series: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 100% (vol/vol in H₂O), each step with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per step)  
4.2 Final dehydration in fresh 100% tert‑butanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.3 Clearing in BB‑PEG solution (benzyl benzoate : polyethylene glycol 400 = 2:1 by volume, RI ~1.56) with gentle shaking. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24–48 hours, until tissue is fully transparent)  

5 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
5.1 Transfer cleared samples into fresh BB‑PEG solution. (Temperature: RT, Time: storage until imaging)  
5.2 Mount in BB‑PEG for light‑sheet or confocal microscopy.

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, NPY antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488, Lectin (IB4) conjugated to DyLight 550, Hoechst 33342]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing of dense, mineralized tissues like bone, achieving high transparency and minimal size shrinkage, which is critical for preserving the intricate 3D architecture of the bone marrow cavity, vasculature, and nerve fibers. It offers excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-derived fluorescence over long imaging periods. The labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goals: TH and NPY antibodies specifically identify sympathetic/peptidergic nerve fibers; IB4 lectin labels the vascular lumen as a structural reference; and Hoechst stains nuclei to map cellular density and define bone marrow compartments.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Sample Preparation and Labeling
1.1 Post-fixation and decalcification in 10% EDTA (pH 7.4) with gentle agitation.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 14 days)
1.2 Permeabilization and blocking in PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100, 0.05% Tween-20, 5% normal donkey serum, and 1% BSA.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
1.3 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-TH (1:500) and goat anti-NPY (1:300) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
1.4 Wash in PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 and 0.05% Tween-20 (PBS-TT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated 4 times)
1.5 Incubation with secondary antibody and lectin cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti-goat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), and IB4 lectin conjugated to DyLight 550 (10 µg/mL) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
1.6 Wash in PBS-TT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, repeated 4 times)
1.7 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
1.8 Final wash in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

2  Dehydration and Delipidation
2.1 Gradual dehydration in a series of tert-butanol (tB) solutions: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% (vol/vol) in water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per step)
2.2 Incubation in 100% anhydrous tB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, repeated twice)
2.3 Delipidation and initial clearing in 100% dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

3  Refractive Index Matching
3.1 Incubation in benzyl benzoate and benzyl alcohol mixture (BBBA, 2:1 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
3.2 Final incubation in pure benzyl benzoate (RI ~1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

4  Mounting and Storage
4.1 Mounting of cleared femur, tibia, and skull bones in fresh benzyl benzoate in an appropriate imaging chamber.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)
4.2 Sealing of the chamber to prevent evaporation and RI change.(Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)
4.3 Storage in the dark at 4 ℃ until imaging.

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH+Alexa Fluor 647, NPY+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS (Polyethylene glycol (PEG)-Associated Solvent System) is explicitly designed for hard, mineralized tissues like bone. It effectively combines decalcification, delipidation, and decolorization in a single, integrated protocol, which is critical for preserving the delicate architecture of the bone marrow cavity and the antigenicity of neural markers like TH and NPY. Its use of tert-butanol and BABB-D4 (dibenzyl ether with hydrogenated additives) ensures excellent clearing of dense bone while maintaining strong fluorescence signals from Alexa Fluor dyes, enabling deep 3D imaging of sympathetic nerve fibers within the hematopoietic niche.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  Decalcification, Dehydration, and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation in 20% (wt/vol) EDTA (pH 7.4) for decalcification.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7-14 days, with solution change every 2 days)
1.2 Wash in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4) to remove EDTA.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 changes)
1.3 Dehydration in a graded tert-butanol (TBA) series: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% (vol/vol in H2O).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per step)
1.4 Delipidation in 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.5 Bleaching in 5% (vol/vol) H2O2 in 100% TBA.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12-24 hours, protected from light)

2  Immunostaining (Passive)
2.1 Rehydration through a reverse graded TBA series: 96%, 90%, 80%, 70%, 50%, 30% (vol/vol in H2O).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
2.2 Wash in 0.01 M PBS (pH 7.4) with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours, with 3 changes)
2.3 Blocking and permeabilization in PBST with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.4 Primary antibody incubation: Rabbit anti-TH (1:500) and Guinea Pig anti-NPY (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72-96 hours, with gentle agitation)
2.5 Wash in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with 6 changes)
2.6 Secondary antibody incubation: Donkey anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Donkey anti-Guinea Pig Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72-96 hours, protected from light, with gentle agitation)
2.7 Wash in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, with 6 changes)
2.8 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours, protected from light)
2.9 Final wash in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours, with 3 changes)

3  Final Dehydration and Refractive Index Matching
3.1 Dehydration in a graded TBA series: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% (vol/vol in H2O).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per step)
3.2 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.3 Refractive Index matching and clearing in BABB-D4 (a hydrogenated, stabilized version of dibenzyl ether, RI ~1.56).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24-48 hours, until fully transparent, stored in the dark)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5 (泛神经标记) + Alexa Fluor 647, α-SMA (肿瘤间质/血管平滑肌) + Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI (核标记)]  
**Justification:** uDISCO 适用于已固定、中等尺寸（~12 mm）的软组织，能实现强脱水、高透明化（RI~1.56）和显著的样本收缩（利于成像大样本），同时能良好保留 Alexa Fluor 等染料荧光。PGP9.5 可标记全部神经纤维（包括轴突），α-SMA 可勾勒肿瘤间质/血管轮廓以辅助判断肿瘤边界与神经的空间关系，DAPI 提供细胞核定位。该方法兼容完整组织块免疫标记，且透明后样本可长期保存于折射率匹配液中。

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 脱水与预通透  
1.1 梯度甲醇脱水：依次在 20%、40%、60%、80%、100%、100% (vol/vol) 甲醇/PBS 溶液中孵育，每步 1 小时。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 每步 1 小时)  
1.2 预通透：在 66% (vol/vol) 二氯甲烷/33% (vol/vol) 甲醇中孵育，温和摇动。(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 小时)  
1.3 再水化：反向梯度甲醇/PBS（100%、80%、60%、40%、20%）孵育，每步 1 小时。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 每步 1 小时)  

2 免疫标记  
2.1 封闭与通透：在含 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100、6% (vol/vol) 驴血清的 PBS 中孵育。(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 小时)  
2.2 一抗孵育：在含 0.2% Triton X-100、3% 驴血清的 PBS 中加入兔抗 PGP9.5 (1:500) 和鼠抗 α-SMA (1:400)，孵育。(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 小时)  
2.3 洗涤：用含 0.2% Triton X-100 的 PBS 洗涤，每天换液 3 次。(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 小时)  
2.4 二抗与 DAPI 孵育：在含 0.2% Triton X-100、3% 驴血清的 PBS 中加入驴抗兔 Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500)、驴抗鼠 Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) 和 DAPI (1 µg/mL)，孵育。(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 小时)  
2.5 洗涤：用含 0.2% Triton X-100 的 PBS 洗涤，每天换液 3 次。(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 小时)  

3 脱水与透明化  
3.1 梯度甲醇脱水：依次在 20%、40%、60%、80%、100%、100% (vol/vol) 甲醇/PBS 中孵育，每步 1 小时。(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 每步 1 小时)  
3.2 四氢呋喃 (THF) 脱水：在 100% (vol/vol) THF 中孵育，每天换液。(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 小时)  

4 折射率匹配与保存  
4.1 浸入二苄醚 (DBE)：将样本转移至 100% (vol/vol) DBE 中。(Temperature: RT, Time: 直至透明，约 12-24 小时)  
4.2 保存与成像：样本可长期保存于新鲜 DBE (RI=1.56) 中，置于避光容器。成像前置于 DBE 填充的成像腔进行光片或共聚焦显微镜三维成像。

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 488, TH+Alexa Fluor 647, Pan-Cytokeratin+Alexa Fluor 555, DAPI]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its excellent clearing depth and high transparency in large, dense tissues (up to ~1 cm³), making it suitable for the 12×8×5 mm pancreatic tumor. It preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes well through its dehydration and delipidation steps. The labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goal: PGP9.5 (Hu C/D) is a pan-neuronal marker for the entire nerve network; TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) is a specific marker for sympathetic adrenergic fibers; Pan-Cytokeratin marks tumor epithelial cells to define tumor boundaries and regions; DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for spatial reference. This combination allows simultaneous 3D visualization and quantitative comparison of pan-neuronal and sympathetic-specific fibers across all regions of interest.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  **Sample Preparation & Permeabilization**
    1.1 Wash fixed tissue in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) for 6 hours, refreshing solution every 2 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
    1.2 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 20% (vol/vol) DMSO) for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
    1.3 Blocking with blocking buffer (PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 6% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, and 10% (vol/vol) DMSO) for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)

2  **Immunolabeling**
    2.1 Primary antibody incubation in antibody buffer (PBS with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide) with the following antibodies: rabbit anti-PGP9.5 (1:500), chicken anti-TH (1:300), mouse anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (1:400). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
    2.2 Wash in PBST with gentle shaking, refreshing wash buffer every 12 hours for a total of 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
    2.3 Secondary antibody incubation in antibody buffer with donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-chicken Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days)
    2.4 Wash in PBST with gentle shaking, refreshing wash buffer every 12 hours for a total of 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
    2.5 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBST for 48 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
    2.6 Final wash in PBST for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3  **Dehydration & Delipidation**
    3.1 Gradual dehydration in a tert-butanol (tB) series: 30% (vol/vol) tB in H₂O, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, each for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 72 hours total)
    3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-butanol for 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
    3.3 Delipidation and clearing in pure dichloromethane (DCM) for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

4  **Refractive Index Matching & Storage**
    4.1 Incubation in pure dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ~1.562) for refractive index matching. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
    4.2 Transfer cleared sample to fresh DBE for storage and imaging. Sample is now ready for light-sheet microscopy. Store in dark at RT.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647 conjugate), CD31 (Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate), Hoechst]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency and strong shrinkage (up to ~65% in volume) in large, dense tissues like whole mouse brain tumors, enabling deep imaging of the entire 8×6×4 mm block. Its organic-solvent-based process preserves fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes exceptionally well and is compatible with lectin perfusion labeling. The shrinkage also increases imaging resolution per voxel. Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647) labels perfused vascular lumens, CD31 (Alexa Fluor 488) labels endothelial cells for structural analysis, and Hoechst labels nuclei for core/edge demarcation and necrosis identification.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Perfusion Labeling and Sample Preparation
1.1 Cardiac perfusion with 1 mg/mL Lectin (Alexa Fluor 647 conjugate) in PBS, 5 mL/min for 5 minutes. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)
1.2 Immediate dissection of the brain with glioma, post-fixation in 4% PFA for 24 hours at 4°C. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Wash samples 3× in PBS, 1 hour each, on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

2  Immunostaining (Optional, if CD31 labeling is required)
2.1 Permeabilization and blocking in PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal donkey serum, and 0.1% sodium azide. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with anti-CD31 primary antibody (1:200 in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.3 Wash 3× in PBS with 0.1% Tween-20 (PBST), 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.4 Incubation with donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488 secondary antibody (1:500 in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.5 Wash 3× in PBST, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
2.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.7 Final wash in PBS, 1 hour. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

3  Dehydration and Delipidation
3.1 Gradual dehydration in tert-butanol (tB) series: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% (vol/vol in H₂O), each step for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 84 hours total)
3.2 Incubation in 100% dichloromethane (DCM) for 3 hours to remove remaining lipids and water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
4.1 Incubation in dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ~1.56) until the tissue is fully transparent (typically 24-48 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
4.2 Optional: For imaging, mount the cleared sample in fresh DBE in a suitable imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: N/A)

**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency and strong shrinkage (preserving morphology while reducing tissue size for easier high-resolution imaging), and it maintains fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes exceptionally well over long periods. Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum lectin) injected intravenously prior to perfusion labels functional, perfused vascular lumens, while CD31 antibody labels all endothelial cells (structural vasculature). Hoechst provides nuclear counterstain for orientation. This dual-channel strategy directly addresses the goal of comparing structural vs. perfused vasculature.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Tissue Preparation and Pre-clearing  
1.1  Wash fixed tissue 3× with PBS, 30 min each, on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours)  
1.2  Dehydrate in a graded methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol (each in PBS), 1 hour per step on a shaker. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours)  
1.3  Incubate in 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.4  Wash 2× with 100% methanol, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2  Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1  Incubate in 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (freshly prepared from 30% stock) for 12 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2  Wash 2× with 100% methanol, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3  Immunostaining (Structural Endothelial Marker)  
3.1  Rehydrate in a descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol in PBS, 1 hour per step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
3.2  Wash 3× with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBS-T), 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
3.3  Block with 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBS-T for 12 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.4  Incubate with primary antibody: anti-CD31 (rat monoclonal, 1:200) in blocking solution for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.5  Wash 6× with PBS-T, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.6  Incubate with secondary antibody: donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and Hoechst 33342 (1:1000) in blocking solution for 48 hours. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
3.7  Wash 6× with PBS-T, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4  Final Dehydration and Clearing  
4.1  Dehydrate again in an ascending methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol (each in PBS), 1 hour per step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 hours)  
4.2  Incubate in 66% (vol/vol) DCM in methanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

4.4  Incubate in 100% (vol/vol) tert-butanol for 3 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.5  Clear in pure dibenzyl ether (DBE, RI ~1.56) with gentle shaking until tissue is transparent (typically 12-24 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)

5.1  Store cleared tissue in fresh DBE in a light-tight container. (Temperature: RT, Time: long-term)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 488, Hoechst]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its superior clearing depth, high transparency, and excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-induced fluorescence in dense, lipid-rich tissues like brain tumors. It is significantly faster than FDISCO and provides uniform clearing. The labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goals: CD31 (PECAM1) is the gold-standard marker for vascular endothelium, allowing structural analysis. Lectin (IB4) binds to glycocalyx of perfused, functional blood vessels, highlighting the perfused lumen. Hoechst provides nuclear counterstain for defining tumor regions. All chosen fluorophores (Alexa Fluor 488/647) are compatible with uDISCO and standard imaging setups.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Immunostaining and Perfusion Marker Labeling (Post-Fixation)
1.1 Permeabilization and Blocking: Incubation with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
1.2 Primary Antibody Incubation: Incubation with anti-CD31 antibody (1:200 dilution) in PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 3% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.3 Wash: Three washes with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours each)
1.4 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Co-Incubation: Incubation with donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated Isolectin GS-IB4 (IB4, 10 µg/mL) in PBST.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
1.5 Nuclear Staining: Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (2 µg/mL) in PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
1.6 Final Wash: Three washes with PBST.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours each)

2  Dehydration (Critical for Uniform Clearing)
2.1 Gradient Methanol Dehydration: Sequential incubation in 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each step)
2.2 Final Dehydration: Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

3  Delipidation and Clearing
3.1 Dichloromethane (DCM) Treatment: Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours) *Do not skip this step.*
3.2 Pure DCM Wash: Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Storage
4.1 uDISCO Clearing Solution: Incubation with Quadrol-based uDISCO solution (prepared as per original publication: Quadrol, 40 wt%; Benzyl Alcohol, 15 vol%; Benzyl Benzoate, 25 vol%; in DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24-48 hours, until tissue is fully transparent)
4.2 Storage and Imaging: Store cleared sample in fresh uDISCO solution in a sealed glass vial.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: Long-term) Image using light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Pan-Cytokeratin (epithelial marker) + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it provides excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescent proteins (especially red-shifted reporters like tdTomato/RFP) and strong tissue shrinkage (~65% volume reduction), which facilitates high-resolution imaging of whole mouse brains. The method is compatible with immunolabeling prior to clearing and yields a high refractive index (RI ~1.56) suitable for light-sheet microscopy. The protocol is relatively fast (days vs. weeks) and maintains structural integrity for spatial analysis of metastasis distribution.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)

2  Refractive Index Matching
2.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, repeated until tissue is transparent)

3  Immunolabeling (Performed after Step 1.4, before Step 1.5)
3.1 Permeabilization and blocking with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, and 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
3.2 Incubation with primary antibody (mouse anti-Pan-Cytokeratin, 1:200) in PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 3% normal donkey serum, and 0.1% sodium azide.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
3.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBS-T).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 4 times)
3.4 Incubation with secondary antibody (donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488, 1:500) in PBS-T with 3% normal donkey serum.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
3.5 Wash with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 4 times)
3.6 Post-fixation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
3.7 Wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)
3.8 Resume dehydration from Step 1.4 (100% methanol).

4  Storage and Imaging
4.1 Store cleared sample in 100% (vol/vol) DBE in a light-tight container at 4 ℃ until imaging.
4.2 Mount sample in uDISCO-compatible chamber filled with DBE for light-sheet microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+
**Chosen Labeling:** [tdTomato (endogenous), Pan-Cytokeratin (antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647), Lectin (DyLight 488 conjugate), DAPI]
**Justification:** iDISCO+ is selected for its excellent clearing of whole mouse brains, strong preservation of endogenous tdTomato/RFP fluorescence, and compatibility with immunolabeling of large, fixed tissues. Its methanol-based dehydration and delipidation effectively clear the brain parenchyma while maintaining structural integrity, which is crucial for analyzing 3D invasion patterns and boundary sharpness. The labeling strategy prioritizes the endogenous tdTomato signal for direct tumor cell localization. The addition of a Pan-Cytokeratin antibody (an epithelial tumor marker) validates the metastatic carcinoma identity. Lectin labels the vasculature to assess perivascular spread, and DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for anatomical context.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)

2  Immunolabeling
2.1 Rehydration through a graded methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
2.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated three times)
2.3 Incubation in permeabilization/blocking solution: PBS with 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.3 M Glycine, and 20% (vol/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24-48 hours)
2.4 Incubation in blocking solution: PBS with 0.2% Tween-20, 0.1% Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum (PBTxD).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Primary antibody incubation: Anti-Pan-Cytokeratin (rabbit, 1:500) and Lectin (DyLight 488 conjugate, 1:200) in PBTxD with 3% donkey serum and 10 µM DAPI.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48-72 hours)
2.6 Wash with PBT (PBS with 0.2% Tween-20).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeated six times over 24 hours)
2.7 Secondary antibody incubation: Donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBT with 3% donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48-72 hours)
2.8 Wash with PBT.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeated six times over 24 hours)

3  Delipidation and Final Dehydration
3.1 Dehydration through a graded methanol series in PBS: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated once)
3.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
4.2 Incubation in dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014).(Temperature: RT, Time: Until tissue is fully cleared and sink, typically 3-6 hours)

**Chosen Method:** BoneClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CGRP+Alexa Fluor 488, TH+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 555]  
**Justification:** BoneClear is specifically optimized for mineralized bone tissue. It integrates decalcification, delipidation, and refractive index matching in a single, gentle aqueous-based workflow, which is critical for preserving the delicate antigenicity of CGRP and TH in nerve fibers within the hard bone matrix. Its compatibility with antibody staining in whole, intact bones makes it ideal for studying 3D nerve distribution in the entire femoral microenvironment (marrow, endosteum, periosteum). The chosen labeling strategy uses primary antibodies against CGRP (sensory) and TH (sympathetic) with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor secondaries, combined with DAPI for nuclei and IB4-lectin (which binds to vascular endothelium and some sensory neurons) to provide contextual vascular architecture.

**Protocol Steps:**
1 Decalcification and Permeabilization
1.1 Incubation with 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 20% (wt/vol) D-sorbitol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days, with daily solution change)
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

2 Immunostaining
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization in PBST containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-CGRP (1:500), mouse anti-TH (1:500), and biotinylated IB4 lectin (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.3 Wash with PBST six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days)
2.5 Wash with PBST six times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)
2.6 Nuclear staining with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.7 Wash with PBST three times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

3 Delipidation and Clearing
3.1 Dehydration in a graded methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water, each step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per step)
3.2 Delipidation in 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.3 Rehydration in a reverse graded methanol series: 100%, 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in distilled water, each step. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per step)
3.4 Final wash in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4 Refractive Index Matching
4.1 Incubation with BoneClear solution (88% (vol/vol) Histodenz, 0.01 M PBS, pH 7.5, RI ~1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours, until tissue is fully transparent)
4.2 Mounting for imaging in fresh BoneClear solution within an imaging chamber.
