1  Tissue Preparation and Fixation
1.1 Perfusion‑fixation of mouse liver with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS via portal vein. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 10 min)
1.2 Post‑fixation of 1‑mm‑thick liver slice in 4% PFA/PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 6 hours)
1.3 Wash with PBS (3 × 10 min). (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 min total)

2  Immunostaining (Sequential)
2.1 Permeabilization and blocking in PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, and 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rat anti‑mouse CD31 (1:200), goat anti‑mouse Stabilin‑2 (1:200), and biotinylated IB4 lectin (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween‑20 (PBS‑T) (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti‑rat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), donkey anti‑goat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), and streptavidin‑Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBS‑T (3 × 1 hour). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)

3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing power and high refractive index (RI ~1.56), which is ideal for high-resolution confocal imaging of thick (500 µm) paraffin sections after rehydration. It provides excellent transparency while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody epitopes. The labeling strategy uses CD3 (pan T-cell marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 and CD8 (cytotoxic T-cell marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 to distinguish T-cell subsets. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstaining to visualize tissue morphology. This combination is compatible with uDISCO's solvent-based dehydration and clearing steps.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Deparaffinization and Rehydration
1.1 Incubation with Xylene (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)
1.2 Incubation with fresh Xylene (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)
1.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)
1.4 Incubation with 95% (vol/vol) Ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)
1.5 Incubation with 70% (vol/vol) Ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)
1.6 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) Ethanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes)
1.7 Rinse with 1x PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes, 3 times)

2  Antigen Retrieval and Permeabilization
2.1 Incubation with pre-heated Citrate Buffer (10 mM Sodium Citrate, 0.05% Tween 20, pH 6.0) (Temperature: 95-100 ℃, Time: 20 minutes)
2.2 Cool down to room temperature naturally (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
2.3 Rinse with 1x PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 5 minutes, 3 times)
2.4 Incubation with Permeabilization/Blocking Buffer (1x PBS, 0.5% Triton X-100, 5% Normal Goat Serum) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

3  Immunofluorescence Staining
3.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail (Anti-CD3 [clone UCHT1] Alexa Fluor 488 conjugate, 1:100; Anti-CD8 [clone C8/144B] Alexa Fluor 647 conjugate, 1:100 in Permeabilization/Blocking Buffer) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
3.2 Rinse with Wash Buffer (1x PBS, 0.1% Triton X-100) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, 4 times)
3.3 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL in 1x PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.4 Rinse with 1x PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes, 3 times)

4  Solvent-Based Dehydration for uDISCO
4.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) Methanol in H2O (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) Methanol in H2O (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) Methanol in H2O (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
4.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, 2 times)

5  uDISCO Clearing
5.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in Methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
5.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, 2 times)
5.3 Incubation with Diethyl Ether (freshly opened) (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)
5.4 Incubation with uDISCO Clearing Solution (85.5% (vol/vol) Diphenyl Ether, 14.5% (vol/vol) Bis(2-ethylhexyl) Phthalate) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12-24 hours until fully transparent)

6  Refractive Index Matching and Mounting
6.1 Transfer cleared tissue into a glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh uDISCO Clearing Solution.
6.2 Seal the dish to prevent evaporation and proceed directly to confocal or light-sheet microscopy.

**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its rapid clearing capability (within 1-2 days), excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescence and immunolabeling signals, and minimal tissue shrinkage/expansion, which is crucial for preserving the delicate 3D architecture of a 300 μm human intestinal organoid. The chosen labeling strategy targets PCNA (proliferating cell nuclear antigen, a DNA replication protein) and Ki67 (a cell cycle-related protein), fulfilling the requirement for dual-protein visualization. Hoechst is used as a nuclear counterstain to delineate all epithelial and non-epithelial nuclei, providing structural context.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
1.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
1.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
1.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

2  Immunolabeling
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Primary antibody incubation with a cocktail of rabbit anti-PCNA (1:200) and mouse anti-Ki67 (1:200) in PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20, 5% (vol/vol) DMSO, and 3% (wt/vol) donkey serum (PBTD).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBTD.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)
2.4 Secondary antibody incubation with a cocktail of donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in PBTD.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBTD.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated 3 times)
2.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.7 Final wash with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes, repeated 2 times)

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) tert-Butanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Diphenyl ether (DPE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Storage
4.1 Transfer to fresh 100% (vol/vol) Diphenyl ether (DPE) for imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO

The chosen markers (NeuN for mature neuronal nuclei, MAP2 for neuronal soma/dendrites) specifically target mature neurons. DAPI provides a general nuclear counterstain. The protocol is adapted for a small, fixed tissue block.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Dehydration and Delipidation
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)

2  Immunostaining (Post-Clearing Labeling)
2.1 Rehydration through a graded methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per step)
2.2 Washing with PBS containing 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated three times)
2.3 Blocking with PBS-T containing 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)
2.4 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: Mouse anti-NeuN (1:500) and Chicken anti-MAP2 (1:1000) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)
2.5 Washing with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated four times)
2.6 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: Donkey anti-Mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and Donkey anti-Chicken IgG Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.7 Washing with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated four times)
2.8 Incubation with DAPI (1 µg/mL) in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.9 Washing with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)

3  Final Dehydration and Clearing
3.1 Dehydration through a graded methanol series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
3.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeated twice)
3.3 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, until tissue is transparent)

**Chosen Labeling:** [α-SMA+Alexa Fluor 647, Collagen IV+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing depth and high transparency in dense tissues like the heart, its strong compatibility with antibody labeling (including for extracellular matrix proteins like Collagen IV), and its excellent preservation of fluorescent protein signals (e.g., from conjugated antibodies). It enables high-resolution 3D imaging of thick (2 mm) cardiac tissue blocks. The chosen labeling strategy directly addresses the scientific goals: α-SMA (Alexa Fluor 647) marks vascular smooth muscle and activated myofibroblasts in fibrotic areas, Collagen IV (Alexa Fluor 488) visualizes the basement membrane of vessels and the remodeled extracellular matrix, and DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for cellular context and spatial orientation.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Fixation
1.1 Perfusion and immersion fixation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Wash tissue block with 0.1 M phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-Tx) 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

2  Immunostaining and Nuclear Labeling
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization in PBS-Tx containing 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-α-SMA (1:500) and goat anti-Collagen IV (1:300) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.3 Wash with PBS-Tx 6 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-goat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.5 Wash with PBS-Tx 6 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)
2.6 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.7 Final wash with PBS 3 times. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)

3  Dehydration and Solvent Transition
3.1 Gradual dehydration in a methanol (MeOH)/PBS series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) MeOH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
3.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) MeOH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated twice)

4  Delipidation and Clearing
4.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) Dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% (vol/vol) MeOH. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM. (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes, repeated twice)

5  Refractive Index Matching and Storage
5.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) Dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, until tissue is fully transparent)
5.2 Store cleared tissue in fresh DBE in a light-tight container for imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** CUBIC  
**Chosen Labeling:** [B220+Alexa Fluor 488, CD19+Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI]  
**Justification:** CUBIC is a hydrophilic clearing method that provides excellent transparency for soft organs like lymph nodes (~3 mm) while preserving endogenous fluorescence and antibody labeling. It is compatible with multi-channel immunostaining and maintains tissue architecture well. The chosen markers B220 (pan-B cell) and CD19 (B cell lineage) together delineate lymphoid follicles and germinal centers, while DAPI labels nuclei for structural reference.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Fixation and Permeabilization  
1.1 Fixation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.3 Permeabilization with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunostaining  
2.1 Blocking with 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: anti-B220 (1:200) and anti-CD19 (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 2 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: goat anti-rat Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 2 hours)  
2.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.7 Final wash with PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Delipidation and Decolorization (CUBIC-L)  
3.1 Incubation with CUBIC-L reagent (25 wt% urea, 25 wt% N,N,N',N'-tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine, 15 wt% Triton X-100 in water). (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
3.2 Refresh CUBIC-L reagent. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching (CUBIC-R+)  
4.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ (45 wt% antipyrine, 30 wt% nicotinamide in water) in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) CUBIC-R+ (RI ~1.52). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Mounting and Imaging  
5.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with fresh CUBIC-R+. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.2 Mount on light-sheet microscope and image with appropriate filter sets for DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, and Alexa Fluor 647.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488, Stabilin-2 antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647, CD31 (PECAM1) antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor 555]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected because it achieves high transparency with minimal tissue deformation (形变不敏感), preserves fluorescence well (保持血管荧光信号), and is compatible with whole adult mouse liver. The labeling strategy uses Lectin (pan-vascular endothelial binding) to label all vessels (肝静脉、门静脉、全肝血管网拓扑), combined with two specific markers: Stabilin-2 (肝血窦内皮细胞特异性受体) and CD31 (PECAM1, general endothelial marker). This dual-target approach ensures肝血窦网络 is not遗漏, while CD31 helps distinguish larger vessels. Alexa Fluor dyes are photostable and compatible with uDISCO’s organic solvent steps.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 固定与通透  
1.1 心脏灌注4% (wt/vol) PFA in PBS (pH 7.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  
1.2 取出整肝，后固定于4% PFA in PBS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 洗涤于PBS (含0.02% 叠氮化钠).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
1.4 通透于PBS含0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 0.05% Tween-20, 0.01% 脱氧胆酸钠.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

2 免疫标记  
2.1 封闭于PBS含5% (vol/vol) 正常驴血清, 0.2% Triton X-100, 0.05% Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 孵育一抗混合物: 抗-Stabilin-2 (1:200), 抗-CD31 (1:200), 凝集素-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) in 封闭液.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 洗涤于PBS含0.2% Triton X-100, 0.05% Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  
2.4 孵育二抗混合物: 驴抗-兔 Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500, 对应Stabilin-2), 驴抗-大鼠 Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500, 对应CD31) in 封闭液.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.5 洗涤于PBS含0.2% Triton X-100, 0.05% Tween-20.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 × 2 hours)  

3 脱水  
3.1 梯度脱水于甲醇/PBS溶液: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) 甲醇, 各步.(Temperature: RT, Time: 各1小时)  
3.2 进一步脱水于100% (vol/vol) 甲醇.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12小时)  

4 脱色与脱脂  
4.1 孵育于新鲜配制的5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 甲醇.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12小时)  
4.2 洗涤于100% (vol/vol) 甲醇.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1小时)  

5 uDISCO透明化  
5.1 孵育于66% (vol/vol) 四氢呋喃 (THF) in H₂O.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1小时)  
5.2 孵育于100% (vol/vol) THF.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1小时)  
5.3 孵育于二氯甲烷 (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 15分钟)  
5.4 孵育于uDISCO储存液: 二苄醚 (DBE) 含0.4% (vol/vol) 四氢呋喃抗氧化剂.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12小时)  

6 折射率匹配与成像前处理  
6.1 将透明肝样本转移至新鲜uDISCO储存液 (DBE+0.4% THF抗氧化剂).(Temperature: RT, Time: 直至成像)  
6.2 将样本置于适合光片显微镜的成像腔室，浸没于uDISCO储存液中进行成像.

**Chosen Labeling:** [Primary Antibody: Nephrin (NPHS1) + Podocin (NPHS2), Secondary Antibody: Alexa Fluor 488 + Alexa Fluor 647, Nuclear Dye: Hoechst, Vascular Probe: Lectin (IB4) - Alexa Fluor 555 conjugate]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its excellent clearing capability in thick tissues (3-4 mm), strong preservation of endogenous fluorescence (crucial for dual-protein assessment), and compatibility with antibody labeling. It achieves high transparency and a high refractive index (RI ~1.56), ideal for deep light-sheet imaging of the whole kidney. The chosen labeling strategy directly targets the two key slit diaphragm proteins (Nephrin and Podocin) to assess glomerular filtration barrier integrity. Hoechst provides a nuclear reference channel, while IB4-lectin labels the vasculature, offering structural context. This combination allows for simultaneous 4-channel observation of podocyte proteins, nuclei, and vessels within the cleared tissue.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Fixation
1.1 Perfusion fixation via left ventricle with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.4).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 10 minutes)
1.2 Post-fixation of dissected whole mouse kidney in fresh 4% PFA.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.3 Washing with 0.1 M phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) with 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBS-T).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 x 1 hour)

2  Immunostaining and Labeling
2.1 Blocking and permeabilization in PBS-T containing 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum and 0.2% (wt/vol) gelatin.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti-Nephrin (1:200) and goat anti-Podocin (1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.3 Washing with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 x 1 hour)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody and probe cocktail: donkey anti-rabbit IgG-Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti-goat IgG-Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), and IB4-lectin-Alexa Fluor 555 (1:100) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)
2.5 Washing with PBS-T.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 x 1 hour)
2.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL Hoechst 33342 in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.7 Washing with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 1 hour)

3  Dehydration and Delipidation
3.1 Gradual dehydration in tert-butanol (tB) series: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 96%, 100% (vol/vol) tB in distilled water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours per step for 30%-90%, 24 hours for 100% tB)
3.2 Delipidation in 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 1 hour)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
4.1 Incubation in uDISCO clearing solution: diphenyl ether (DPE) with 5% (vol/vol) tetrahydronaphthalene (Tetralin) as antioxidant.(Temperature: RT, Time: Until tissue is transparent, minimum 48 hours)
4.2 Storage and imaging in fresh uDISCO solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinitely)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [Hoechst, Lectin (凝集素), alpha-bungarotoxin]
**Justification:** uDISCO provides exceptional transparency and shrinkage, ideal for dense, whole E14 mouse embryos. It preserves endogenous fluorescence (e.g., GFP/YFP) and is compatible with lipophilic dye labeling. Hoechst provides a universal nuclear counterstain for anatomical registration. Lectin labels vasculature and specific glycans, outlining tissue architecture. Alpha-bungarotoxin specifically labels nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, crucial for identifying neuromuscular junctions and early peripheral nerve innervation patterns, complementing the neural structure analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Fixation and Pre-treatment
1.1  Perfusion and immersion fixation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (PB), pH 7.4.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)
1.2  Wash with 0.1 M PB containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBTx).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 1 hour)
1.3  Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) and 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in 0.1 M PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)

2  Fluorescent Labeling
2.1  Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated alpha-bungarotoxin (2 µg/mL) and Fluorescein-conjugated Lectin (e.g., WFA, 10 µg/mL) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle shaking)
2.2  Wash with PBTx to remove unbound probes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 x 1 hour)
2.3  Incubation with Hoechst 33342 (5 µg/mL) in PBTx for nuclear staining.(Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)
2.4  Final wash with 0.1 M PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 1 hour)

3  Dehydration and Delipidation
3.1  Gradual dehydration in a methanol (MeOH)/water series: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) MeOH in water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per step)
3.2  Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) MeOH.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 x 1 hour)
3.3  Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) / 33% (vol/vol) MeOH.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.4  Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 x 15 minutes)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
4.1  Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014-1KG).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 x 1 hour)
4.2  Final storage and imaging in fresh DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: until imaging)

**Chosen Labeling:** [CD45+Alexa Fluor 647, Ly6G+Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its exceptional clearing of dense, mineralized tissues like bone, achieving high transparency and a high refractive index (RI ~1.56) compatible with light-sheet microscopy. The chosen labeling strategy uses a pan-immune cell marker (CD45) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 to label all immune cells, and a myeloid subset marker (Ly6G for neutrophils) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488. DAPI is used for nuclear counterstaining. uDISCO preserves the fluorescence of these Alexa Fluor dyes well, enabling robust 3D visualization.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Tissue Preparation and Decalcification
1.1 Post-fixation with 4% (wt/vol) PFA in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Decalcification with 10% (wt/vol) EDTA in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, with gentle shaking.(Temperature: RT, Time: 7 days)
1.3 Rinse with 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, three times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

2  Immunofluorescence Staining
2.1 Permeabilization and blocking with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 and 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rat anti-mouse CD45 (1:200) and rat anti-mouse Ly6G (1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.3 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, five times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rat IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 7 days)
2.5 Wash with 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, five times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours each)
2.6 Nuclear staining with 1 µg/mL DAPI in 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
2.7 Final wash with 0.1 M PBS, pH 7.4, three times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)

3  Dehydration and Delipidation
3.1 Dehydration with a graded methanol series in PBS: 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% (vol/vol) methanol, each step.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours each)

3.3 Second delipidation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
4.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
4.2 Transfer to fresh 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE) for final clearing and storage.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

**Chosen Method:** PEGASOS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [IB4 (lectin, pre-perfused vascular lumen signal), Osteocalcin (for osteoblast-secreted matrix protein), Osx/Osterix (for osteoblast-lineage cells), DAPI (for nuclei)]  
**Justification:** PEGASOS (Polyethylene glycol‑Associated Solvent System) is selected because it is explicitly designed for hard tissues like bone, effectively clearing mineralized bone while preserving endogenous fluorescence and pre‑existing labels (e.g., lectin/IB4). It uses a graded organic‑solvent dehydration and delipidation that minimizes structural collapse and avoids harsh decalcification, thus protecting the delicate bone‑trabecular and vascular architecture. The method ends with a high‑refractive‑index, non‑hazardous mounting medium (BB‑PEG) suitable for high‑resolution 3D imaging (light‑sheet/confocal). The chosen labeling strategy uses the pre‑existing IB4 for vasculature, Osteocalcin to distinguish secreted bone matrix, and Osx/Osterix to label osteoblast‑lineage cells, allowing simultaneous 3D visualization of all three targets.

**Protocol Steps:**

1  **Dehydration & Decalcification**  
1.1 Incubation in 20% (wt/vol) EDTA (pH 7.4) in PBS with gentle agitation. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.2 Wash in PBS 3 times, 30 min each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours)  
1.3 Incubation in 30% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.4 Incubation in 50% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.5 Incubation in 70% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.6 Incubation in 95% (vol/vol) ethanol in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.7 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) ethanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, repeated once)

2  **Delipidation & Bleaching (optional)**  
2.1 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) with gentle agitation. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
2.2 Incubation in fresh 100% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
2.3 Optional bleaching step if autofluorescence is high: Incubation in 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.4 If bleaching was performed, re‑dehydrate through graded ethanol series (70%, 95%, 100%, 100%) for 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT)

3  **Refractive‑Index Matching & Clearing**  
3.1 Incubation in 50% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate (BB) in ethanol. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation in 100% (vol/vol) benzyl benzoate (BB). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation in BB‑PEG clearing solution (benzyl benzoate : polyethylene glycol 400 = 2:1 by volume, RI ≈ 1.56). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)

4  **Immunolabeling (if required for Osteocalcin/Osx)**  
*Note: If the sample already carries the pre‑perfused IB4 signal and endogenous Osteocalcin/Osx fluorescence is sufficient, skip to step 5. If immunostaining is needed, perform after step 1.7 (ethanol dehydration) and before step 2.1 (DCM).*  
4.1 Rehydrate sample through descending ethanol series (95%, 70%, 50%, 30%) to PBS, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT)  
4.2 Permeabilization and blocking: Incubation in PBS containing 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X‑100, 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, and 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.3 Primary antibody incubation: Incubation in blocking solution containing rabbit anti‑Osteocalcin (1:200) and goat anti‑Osx/Osterix (1:200). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
4.4 Wash in PBS with 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween‑20 (PBST) 6 times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT)  
4.5 Secondary antibody incubation: Incubation in blocking solution containing donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:500) and donkey anti‑goat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  
4.6 Wash in PBST 6 times, 2 hours each. (Temperature: RT)  
4.7 Nuclear counterstain: Incubation in 1 µg/mL DAPI in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
4.8 Wash in PBS 3 times, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT)  
4.9 Proceed to dehydration (step 1.3–1.7) and then continue with delipidation (step 2.1).

5  **Storage & Imaging**  
5.1 Store cleared sample in BB‑PEG solution (RI ≈ 1.56) in a light‑tight container. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: long‑term)  
5.2 For imaging, mount sample in BB‑PEG in an appropriate imaging chamber (e.g., quartz cuvette or custom 3D‑printed holder) and image using light‑sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [PGP9.5+Alexa Fluor 488, TH+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (IB4)+Alexa Fluor 555]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is selected for its excellent clearing of dense, mineralized tissues (including bone and teeth), strong fluorescence preservation of Alexa Fluor dyes through organic solvent dehydration, and compatibility with whole-organ 3D imaging. The labeling strategy uses PGP9.5 (pan-neuronal marker, Hu C/D/PGP9.5) to label all nerve fibers, TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) to specifically label sympathetic fibers, and IB4 lectin (which binds to vascular endothelium and some sensory neurons) to provide a vascular reference channel. This combination allows simultaneous 3D visualization of hard tissue, pulp soft tissue, general innervation, sympathetic innervation, and vasculature.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1  Dehydration and Delipidation  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)  
1.6 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
1.7 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  

2  Immunostaining (Optional pre‑bleaching with H2O2 may be added before Step 1 if autofluorescence is high)  
2.1 Incubation with permeabilization/blocking solution: PBS with 0.2% Triton X‑100, 0.3 M glycine, 20% DMSO, and 5% normal donkey serum (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 days)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rabbit anti‑PGP9.5 (1:500), rabbit anti‑TH (1:500), and biotinylated IB4 lectin (10 µg/mL) in PBS with 0.2% Triton X‑100, 10% DMSO, and 3% normal donkey serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
2.3 Wash with PBS containing 0.2% Tween‑20 and 10 µg/mL heparin (PTwH) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 4 times)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500), donkey anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500), and streptavidin Alexa Fluor 555 (1:500) in PTwH with 3% normal donkey serum (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days)  
2.5 Wash with PTwH (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat 4 times)  

3  Final Dehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour, repeat once)  

4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing  
4.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 15 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours, repeat once until tissue is fully cleared)  

5  Mounting and Imaging  
5.1 Transfer cleared molar into fresh DBE in an imaging‑compatible chamber.  
5.2 Image using light‑sheet or confocal microscopy with appropriate filter sets for Alexa Fluor 488, 555, and 647.

The chosen labeling strategy uses two distinct antibodies against Brn3a and Brn3b (POU4F family transcription factors) to fulfill the requirement for dual RGC identity verification, coupled with IB4 lectin for simultaneous retinal vasculature labeling. uDISCO's final refractive index (RI ~1.56) is compatible with high-resolution imaging.

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD8-Alexa Fluor 647, CD3-Alexa Fluor 488, DAPI]
**Justification:** uDISCO is chosen for its excellent clearing of pigmented tissues, strong quenching of endogenous melanin autofluorescence, and high transparency with good preservation of fluorescent protein signals. The dual-labeling strategy using CD8 (cytotoxic T cell marker) and CD3 (pan-T cell marker) allows for the specific identification and distinction of CD8+ T cells within the broader T cell population at the dermal-epidermal junction. DAPI provides nuclear counterstain for structural context. This combination is compatible with uDISCO's solvent-based dehydration and clearing steps.

**Protocol Steps:**
1  Fixation and Pre-treatment
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (PB).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)
1.2 Washing with 0.1 M PB containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBTx).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 1 hour)
1.3 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum (NDS) and 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in 0.1 M PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)
2  Immunofluorescence Labeling
2.1 Incubation with primary antibody cocktail: rat anti-mouse CD8α (1:200) and rabbit anti-human CD3 (1:200) in blocking solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.2 Washing with PBTx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 x 1 hour)
2.3 Incubation with secondary antibody cocktail: donkey anti-rat IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) in blocking solution.(Temperature: RT, Time: 48 hours)
2.4 Washing with PBTx.(Temperature: RT, Time: 6 x 1 hour)
2.5 Incubation with 1 µg/mL DAPI in 0.1 M PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)
2.6 Washing with 0.1 M PB.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 x 30 minutes)
3  Dehydration and Delipidation
3.1 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in deionized water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.2 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in deionized water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.3 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in deionized water.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)
3.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 x 1 hour)
3.5 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) and 33% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)
3.6 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 x 15 minutes)
4  Refractive Index Matching and Clearing
4.1 Incubation with dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma 108014) containing 0.5% (wt/vol) 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenol (BHT) as antioxidant.(Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)
